Ugandan police are investigating the deaths of four pupils at a school in the capital Kampala which they suspect may be the result of poisoning.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the four girls, aged between nine and 11 years, died on tuesday. Three of the pupils died at home while the fourth passed away while receiving emergency treatment at a hospital.

The head teacher at the school, Ta'aliim Primary School and Quran Memorisation Centre, has been arrested to assist with investigations.

According to the school, eight pupils had eaten oranges shared by a fellow pupil.

Berdasarkan laporan, five pupils, including the four who later died, started vomiting. The fifth is still in hospital.

Post-mortem examinations are being carried out to determine the exact cause of death.

A police spokesperson was quoted by local media as saying that detectives would visit the village where the oranges the pupils ate came from.

The centre has been cordoned off as a crime scene.

Ugandan media shared videos of grieving parents describing their children's final moments, with some accusing the school of failing to provide clear and timely information.

The police have offered condolences to the bereaved families and affected community and say more information will be provided in due course.

The tragedy comes at a time when concerns are mounting over health and safety conditions in schools across Uganda.

Previous cases involving suspected contaminated food and exposure to harmful substances have left pupils hospitalised with symptoms including stomach pain, vomiting and breathing difficulties.

The incidents have intensified calls for authorities to strengthen monitoring of school feeding schemes, improve hygiene standards and ensure safer learning environments for children.

De la Espriella said he had personally authorised the bombing targeting the Gulf Clan in the province of Antioquia, in north-west Colombia.

He added that Haminton Mosquera, whom he described as a senior member of the crime gang and one of 10 "priority targets" for Colombia's security forces, had been "brought down".

De la Espriella was elected in June after campaigning on a promise to crack down on Colombia's powerful criminal gangs, including by launching air strikes.

The Gulf Clan has been engaging in criminal activities for decades, mainly trafficking cocaine from Colombia to destinations in the US and Europe but also illegal mining and people smuggling.

The US added it to its list of Foreign Terrorist Organisations (FTOs) last year.

In his post, President de la Espriella said that "the offensive won't stop" and vowed to regain control of areas currently controlled by criminal organisations such as the Gulf Clan.

While his offensive against criminal gangs has been welcomed by many living in areas where extortion and gang violence are rampant, de la Espriella has faced criticism for the way he has made some of his announcements on security.

#79. China rules out hosting Cop33 climate summit in 2028

📅 12 Nov 2026

China rules out hosting Cop33 climate summit in 2028

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/12/china-rules-out-hosting-cop33-climate-summit-in-2028

Decision disappoints experts hoping for world’s biggest emitter to take global lead on climate crisis.

China has ruled out hosting the Cop33 UN climate summit in 2028 after months of deliberations, leaving the field open for other Asian countries to hold it, the Guardian understands.

The decision will disappoint many countries and climate experts, who had hoped the world’s biggest emitter would take the lead on the global stage, as the US under Donald Trump has vacated all forms of international cooperation on the climate.

Diungkapkan bahwa al gore, the former us vice-president, was among those left disheartened by the decision. “I would be very much in favour of that idea [of China hosting the summit],” he told the Guardian. “It’s too bad. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, china is in the midst of an economic transformation, from being heavily dependent on coal to becoming an “electro state”. John Kerry, the former US secretary of state, told the Guardian that China was leaving the rest of the world behind in forging and using the low-carbon technologies of the future.

Renewable energy generation capacity has now outstripped coal in China, and its greenhouse gas emissions appear to have declined slightly this year.

Sales of electric vehicles in the country have also taken off, making up nearly two-thirds of the market last month, and China’s clean energy industries drove more than 90% of the country’s investment growth last year.

The rules of the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) mean an Asian country should host in 2028.

Gareth Redmond-King, the international lead at the Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit thinktank, said China’s position as an industrial powerhouse would have made it a formidable contender to hold the summit.

“It would undoubtedly be significant for the world’s biggest emitter and second-biggest economy to host a climate Cop,” he said.

Berdasarkan laporan, “they’re leading the world on investment, manufacture and deployment of clean energy tech, and their emissions have started to tick down. As a leadership story, China hosting Cop33 would be a big deal. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it is not clear why china has decided against hosting the conference, but several experts that spoke to the guardian suggested that the us electoral cycle was likely to have been a factor. The next US presidential election will take place on 7 November 2028, and Cop33 is scheduled for 6 to 17 November that year.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, after the strong showing by democrats in the recent midterm elections, in which voter concern over the climate crisis was thought to be a factor, the democrats will be hoping to elect a climate-friendly president in 2028. But even if they succeed, Trump will still be in office until the following January.

The US president rejects climate science and withdrew the US from the Paris agreement, and is also withdrawing from its parent treaty, the 1992 UNFCCC.

Diungkapkan bahwa the planet's most important stories. Get all the week's environment news - the good, the bad and the essential.

Berdasarkan laporan, china seeks to be seen as a leader among developing countries, but has been wary of stepping into the gap left by the us. Under the Democratic presidents Joe Biden and Barack Obama, the US and China enjoyed a close partnership on climate issues, setting joint targets on reducing methane and developing clean technology.

Diungkapkan bahwa cop33 will be an important meeting because it will include the “global stocktake” – a mechanism under the 2015 paris climate agreement that examines countries’ progress on cutting emissions in line with the goal of limiting global temperature rises to 1. 5C.

That limit is now certain to be surpassed, but experts say countries should now try to minimise the temperature “overshoot”, to avoid worse ravages from extreme weather.

Sebagaimana diketahui, india’s government considered offering to host cop33 for several months earlier this year, but also decided against it. India’s coal use has been increasing, even as the country exceeds its own renewable energy targets.

The Guardian understands that other countries mulling a bid to host Cop33 include Uzbekistan, South Korea, Indonesia and Thailand.

The woman disappeared while on the Marella Voyager (file photo).

The search for a British woman who is believed to have gone overboard from a cruise ship while it was crossing the Atlantic has been suspended, the US Coast Guard (USCG) has said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the 72-year-old was last seen aboard tui's marella voyager on monday while the vessel was en route to the caribbean. Staff realised she was missing on Tuesday, when they noticed her "bed untouched".

USCG said the ship was approximately 500 nautical miles from the area where she was believed to entered the water when it received a missing report.

It added that a coordinated international search and rescue effort had been called off on Wednesday due to factors including "the low likelihood of survival".

Diungkapkan bahwa uscg said the woman was last recorded accessing a cabin door at about midday on monday. She is believed to have gone overboard in a remote area of the North Atlantic, roughly 1,400 nautical miles from Bermuda.

In a previous statement, Tui said that after staff realised she was missing, the alarm was raised and a search carried out.

The Daily Mail earlier reported that holidaymakers on board the ship had been told to abandon dinners, drinks and entertainment as the crew carried out an emergency headcount on Tuesday evening.

Passengers stood in lines of four while staff scanned boarding cards to verify the identity of every person on the ship, according to the newspaper.

In a statement, USCG confirmed it had received a missing report at about 19:30 EST (00:30 GMT) on Tuesday.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the coast guard said staff also reported that the marella did not have enough fuel to return to the search area. It is understood that USCG asked the ship to continue its crossing rather than reverse course and search for the woman.

It said that volunteers from the coast guard then worked with search and rescue partners including the Maritime Rescue Coordination Center Delgada and the UK's Joint Rescue Coordination Centre, and issued urgent maritime broadcasts requesting assistance from ships in the area.

It added that multiple commercial vessels were contacted as part of the operation to "consider search opportunities, but none were in the vicinity".

Search efforts were suspended at about 15:50 EST (20:50 GMT) on Wednesday, "after considering the extensive search area, the elapsed time between the presumed incident and notification, the lack of available search assets in the remote location, negative results from maritime broadcasts, the sea state, and the low likelihood of survival", the coast guard said.

The Marella Voyager, carrying around 2,000 passengers and 800 crew, left Malaga on 4 November and is due to arrive in Antigua on Friday before calling at Dominica and finishing its voyage in Barbados on Sunday.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a spokeswoman for marella cruises earlier said it was supporting the authorities with their enquiries. It added it was "deeply saddened" by the disappearance, adding: "Our thoughts are with the guest's loved ones at this very difficult time.

Berdasarkan laporan, a uk foreign office spokesperson said in an earlier statement: "we are supporting the family of a british national reported missing on a cruise ship in the atlantic ocean and we are in touch with the relevant authorities. ".

In a separate case, a cruise ship pianist was found treading water on Sunday around 20 miles off the Californian coast after falling overboard.

Two fishermen discovered the Royal Caribbean employee near Catalina Island and officials believe he may have been in the Pacific Ocean for nine hours, according to CBS News, the BBC's US news partner.

Clashes have broken out between groups of masked men and police in Barcelona after tens of thousands of people took part in Spain's first general strike for 14 years, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living.

Some 120,000 people joined a demonstration in the capital Madrid and more than 50,000 turned out in Barcelona, where footage showed masked men setting fire to rubbish bins and smashing shop windows as police fired tear gas.

Transport and other public services across Spain faced serious disruption.

Spaniards are due to vote in parliamentary elections on 29 November.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the head of the big ugt labour union, pepe ãlvarez, said the strike was a success with "massive" participation, while unai sordo of the cc oo union said turnout was "very significant. ".

Some of the disturbances took place in the Passeig de GrÃ cia, close to the iconic PlaÃ§a de Catalunya in the centre of the city.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the bbc spoke to a woman who attended the protests in barcelona who said it was mostly very peaceful and "joyful". She said she was there to protest about the housing costs and that "there were a lot of children and old people there. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, she was in the area of las ramblas in the evening and saw fires in the streets. "The fires were everywhere, it was very intense," she said.

Earlier in the day there was major disruption around Madrid and Barcelona, with traffic halted on several main roads.

The interior ministry said dozens of people were arrested for a variety of incidents and Spanish reports said estate agencies had seen attacks on their offices.

Police said they had made dozens of arrests.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we've completely brought the city to a standstill," a protester in madrid told reuters news agency, adding there was widespread support for the general strike. "Everyone's out there, despite the rainy weather; everyone's out on the streets. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, another protester, 37-year-old teacher olga domingo, said she was protesting because "the housing situation is outrageous. The current cost of living compared to wages is completely unsustainable".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the strike was triggered by widespread protests over affordable housing and rising living costs, after the eviction of 87-year-old maricarmen abascal from a flat in madrid where she had lived for seven decades. She died in hospital weeks later.

Sebagaimana diketahui, rental prices in the capital have risen in recent years. The monthly cost of a 50 sq m apartment in Madrid was an average of â¬1,170 ($1,300; Â£1,000) in October, according to property portal Idealista, while Spain's average gross monthly salary is about â¬2,460.

That amounts to nearly half the average gross salary, well above the 30% level of affordability often recommended by housing experts and public institutions.

Watch: Protesters gather across Spain for first general strike in 14 years.

Socialist Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez called snap elections last month after parliament failed to approve his plan for housing reform.

Not since 2012, under the conservative government of Mariano Rajoy, has Spain held general strikes.

Berdasarkan laporan, and while previous strikes have been problematic for the government in power, this one is different. SÃ¡nchez and his ministers have even encouraged workers to down tools and demand affordable housing.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "your eight-hour day. Your pension. Your public healthcareâ¦ These were collective conquests," he wrote on social media, praising those who took part in previous strikes.

Tyres were set on fire in the city of Gijon in northern Spain.

The conservative People's Party (PP), by contrast, has accused the government of attempting to weaponise the strike for electoral gain.

Sebagaimana diketahui, pp leader alberto nãºã±ez feijã³o called the general strike "nonsense", calling the unions "mafia" and "trash". Feijoo's party is leading in the polls and party spokesman Miguel Tellado accused the government of exploiting the strike to warn voters against allowing a right-wing government to be formed, which looks the most likely outcome of the 29 November election.

Diungkapkan bahwa sã¡nchez told spanish tv this week: "what is nonsense is to question the rights of workers to strike. ".

Among those taking part in the general strike was Gonzalo Ãlvarez, 27, who was visiting different picket lines in central Madrid.

Although he works in sales, he has been volunteering for a housing union that tries to protect tenants and makes them aware of their rights.

The eviction of Maricarmen Abascal at the end of September "was the little fire" that sparked this protest, he told the BBC.

Ãlvarez knew the 87-year-old, who had faced a tripling of her rent under new landlords, and says he was deeply upset by her treatment.

Berdasarkan laporan, he rents a small, one-bedroom flat with his girlfriend, a dental hygienist, in the city's southern arganzuela disrict. The couple pay â¬1,000 between them, which means each spends about half of their salary on housing, even before other bills.

Berdasarkan laporan, "it's absolutely crazyâ¦ with the food, with the electricity, with the water, with gas. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa he sees no way of getting on the property ladder: "you have to collect an insane amount of money to be able to buy a house. So with these salaries, it's impossible. ".

With current rent and purchase prices, he believes buying somewhere is "completely impossible".

Gonzalo Ãlvarez, who was taking part in the general strike, says 50% of his salary goes towards rent.

However, the vice-president of the CEOE, Spanish biggest business association, Miguel Garrido, criticised the strike, complaining that businesses had little to do with the price of housing.

"This is not a strike for labour-related reasons, but rather for political ones, and it is closely linked to the early calling of elections," he said.

Demonstrations were planned for some of Spain's biggest cities later in the day and the scale of support will be widely viewed as an indicator of public discontent ahead of the election.

Another reliable indicator of support for strikes is the level of demand for electricity with Spain's industrial sector.

Berdasarkan laporan, power usage in spain fell by 7. 5% during the early hours of Wednesday, according to data from operator Red ElÃ©ctrica. During the last general strike 14 years ago, equivalent consumption was down by more than 15%.

Sebagaimana diketahui, our live coverage for the day has ended. Follow the latest Ukraine news here or read through the updates below.

Berdasarkan laporan, the preventive detention hearing for daria trepova, who was detained in connection with the explosion at a cafe in st. Petersburg, Russia, will take place on Tuesday at Basmanny District Court in Moscow, according to Russian state news agency Vesti.

Berdasarkan laporan, russian authorities detained trepova, 26, claiming she was involved in the blast that killed well-known military blogger vladlen tatarsky at a café in st. Petersburg on Sunday.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the us ambassador to the united nations linda thomas-greenfield on monday described russia assuming the united nations security council (unsc) presidency this month as “an april fool’s joke. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “but the truth of the matter is, it’s a rotating seat. We expect that they will behave professionally. But we also expect that they will use their seat to spread disinformation and to promote their own agenda as it relates to Ukraine, and we will stand ready to call them out at every single moment that they attempt to do that,” Greenfield added.

Greenfield said she is not surprised if the Russians asked the foreign minister to come to UNSC headquarters in New York but also said council does work beyond Ukraine.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we haven’t decided yet on what our attendance levels will be, but we intend to carry out the business of the security council during this month. The Security Council does more than Ukraine. We work on many issues, and we again expect that Russia will carry their presidency in a professional way, but when they don’t, we will stand ready to call them out,” Greenfield said.

Vasily Nebenzya, Russian ambassador to the United Nations, dismissed concerns that Russia could fairly be the president of the Security Council for April during the ongoing war in Ukraine.

He said there were no complaints in February 2022 when Russia was last president of the council, while Russia invaded and pointed out that the US was president of the council in 2003 — the year Iraq was invaded.

The ambassador said as long as world order is maintained, there will not be any change in UN procedures that might lead to a change in Russia’s status.

Newly published video shows the moments running up to an explosion that killed Russian military journalist Vladen Tartovsky in a St Petersburg café on Sunday.

Sebagaimana diketahui, tatarsky died when a blast tore through the cafe where he was appearing as a guest of a pro-war group called cyber front z. Prior Russian media reports suggested that Tatarsky may have been killed by a device hidden in a figurine presented to him by a woman before the blast.

The 25-second video shows Tartovsky putting a statuette given to him at the event into a box after passing the microphone to another man.

Berdasarkan laporan, he places the statuette back into the box and then covers it with what appears to be paper wrapping. As he presses down the paper, there is an explosion.

In the last two seconds of the video, Tartovsky is pixillated, but the rest of the scene is not.

More to know: The well-known Russian blogger was killed in what appeared to be an audacious attack on a high-profile pro-Kremlin figure, officials said.

Authorities said they were treating the case as suspected murder.

At least 32 people were injured in the blast, with 10 people in serious condition, state media Ria Novosti reported, citing the Russian Ministry of Health.

Russian ambassador to the United Nations Vasily Nebenzya on Monday scoffed at concerns that his country could fairly be the president of the Security Council for April during the war in Ukraine.

Nebenzya pointed out that the US was president of the council in 2003 — the year Iraq was invaded.

He said there were no complaints in February 2022 when Russia was last president of the council, while Russia invaded.

The ambassador said as long as world order is maintained, there will not be any change in UN procedures that might lead to a change in Russia’s status.

Russia took over presidency on Saturday of the UN’s top security body, which rotates every month.

Diungkapkan bahwa ukraine has received the first tranche of $2. 7 billion from a new International Monetary Fund (IMF) program, Ukrainian Finance Minister Sergii Marchenko said in a tweet Monday.

Diungkapkan bahwa the imf, which regularly makes emergency loans to countries in crisis, on friday approved a new four-year extended arrangement under the extended fund facility (eff) of around $15. 6 billion as part of a $115 billion total support package for Ukraine.

The program aims to “anchor policies that sustain fiscal, external, price and financial stability and support economic recovery, while enhancing governance and strengthening institutions to promote long-term growth in the context of post-war reconstruction and Ukraine’s path to EU accession,” the IMF said in a statement.

The program also helps Ukraine to carry out “more ambitious structural reforms,” it said.

The Extended Fund Facility (EFF) loan is the first major conventional financing program approved by the IMF for a country involved in a large-scale war, Reuters reported.

The risks to the arrangement are “exceptionally high,” said Gita Gopinath, first deputy managing director of the global lender.

“The success of the program depends on the size, composition, and timing of external financing on concessional terms to help close fiscal and external financing gaps and restore debt sustainability on a forward-looking basis under the baseline and downside scenarios,” she added.

German Chancellor Olaf Scholz on Monday assured Moldova of Berlin’s support on its path to accession to the European Union as Moldovan and American officials allege Russia of trying to weaken the government in Chisinau.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “moldova is part of our european family. In the summer, we granted it candidate status. And I very much welcome how resolutely Moldova has tackled the necessary reforms that are indispensable for EU accession,” Scholz told a news conference in Bucharest, Romania alongside Romanian President Klaus Iohannis and Moldovan President Maia Sandu.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “moldova can be sure of our support on this path. I assured the President [Sandu] of this once again today. Moldova does not stand alone, but receives massive international support,” the German chancellor continued.

Berdasarkan laporan, scholz expressed “great concern” about reports of alleged russian attempts to destabilize moldova and said germany would do its “utmost” to support moldova in arming itself against “attempts of destabilization by russia. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa in february, moldova’s president sandu accused russia of planning to use “saboteurs who have undergone military training and are disguised as civilians” to destabilize the country — claims which were rejected by russia’s foreign ministry as “unfounded. ”.

According to White House officials, the US believes that Russia is working to weaken the Moldovan government, as it continues to seek closer ties with the European Union.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the sovereignty and territorial integrity of any state is inviolable. This requirement of the Helsinki Final Act and other agreements under international law was also signed by Russia. And it is still valid. Therefore, we do our utmost to support Moldova in arming itself against attempts of destabilization by Russia,” Scholz said.

Berdasarkan laporan, speaking at the same event, sandu said that “it is very important, and i am happy that moldova is a dialogue partner with romania and germany. The projects we are involved in together are very useful for our people and will strongly lead us to the accession (to the European Union). ”.

CNN’s Radina Gigova, Anna Chernova and Natasha Bertrand contributed reporting to this post.

NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg said Monday that the alliance has not seen any changes in Russia’s nuclear posture since Russian President Vladimir Putin announced late last month Moscow’s plans to station tactical nuclear weapons in neighboring Belarus.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we monitor very closely what russia does. But so far, we haven’t seen any changes in their nuclear posture that requires any change in our nuclear posture,” the NATO chief said, while answering questions from reporters on the topic at a news conference in Brussels.

Diungkapkan bahwa stoltenberg described putin’s announcement as a “pattern of dangerous, reckless nuclear rhetoric. ”.

“President Putin tries to use nuclear weapons as a way to prevent us from supporting Ukraine… intimidation, coercion to stop NATO Allies and partners for supporting Ukraine in their right to defend their own country,” he said.

Berdasarkan laporan, “we will not be intimidated. We will continue to support Ukraine,” Stoltenberg continued.

NATO’s chief Jens Stoltenberg said on Monday that Western allies have delivered more than $70 billion in military aid to Ukraine over the last year since the Russian invasion started.

Diungkapkan bahwa “there are no signs that president putin is preparing for peace. He is preparing for more war,” Stoltenberg warned, speaking at a news conference in Brussels.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we do not know when this war will end. And history does not repeat itself. But when it does, we will need to put in place arrangements so that Ukraine can deter future aggression. We cannot allow Russia to continue to chip away at European security,” he said.

Diungkapkan bahwa stoltenberg added that allies have delivered 65 billion euros (around $70. 7 billion) in military aid, and said he welcomed the recent arrival of modern battle tanks and other armored vehicles in Ukraine.

“This can make a real difference on the front lines and allow the Ukrainian forces to liberate more territory,” he said.

Berdasarkan laporan, the nato head affirmed that the alliance’s support is for the “long haul” and said, “we will discuss how we can step up our support, including by continuing to strengthen ukraine’s armed forces and supporting the transition from soviet-era to nato equipment and doctrine. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, stoltenberg also said allies must address other threats and challenges, citing instability, terrorism, and the growing influence of iran, russia, and china. He urged allies to invest more in defense to tackle all these wide range of issues.

Norway and Denmark will cooperate to donate 8,000 artillery rounds to Ukraine, the Norwegian government announced in a statement on Monday.

Berdasarkan laporan, oleksandr syrskyi, commander of ukrainian land forces, posted on telegram that in bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the wagner fighters and russian paratroopers. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of donetsk – as the russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge ukrainian defenses in avdiivka and mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

Diungkapkan bahwa “there are also some operational successes of our military in the donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the enemy is trying to attack our positions between avdiivka and marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

Diungkapkan bahwa “it is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… after clearing kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

Diungkapkan bahwa the war in ukraine has cost an estimated $2. 6 billion of damage to heritage and cultural sites in the country, the UN cultural body UNESCO said in a recently published report.

Berdasarkan laporan, reporters and sleuths on chinese social media have been trying to get to the bottom of who the megaspeed chief really is. On Tuesday, the Financial Times published an interesting report (£) about Alice Huang’s backstory. She was born in the rural area of Hunan, worked as a journalist at China’s state broadcaster, then at HSBC and the investment bank Citic Securities. In 2015, she joined an investment management company Hexi.

Berdasarkan laporan, there, she met financier kang wei. The two became romantically involved, and together they reinvented themselves as AI entrepreneurs. In 2023, Huang and her business partners acquired Megaspeed, a Singaporean subsidiary of a Chinese gaming company, which she and Wei aimed to turn into a datacentre business. According to the FT’s report, the two pitched investors on their ability to secure access to Nvidia chips.

Diungkapkan bahwa nobody knows exactly when jensen huang met alice huang, when their relationship became romantic, or what information she might have passed to beijing while it was going on. As Aisha Down and Dan Milmo pointed out earlier this week, Jensen Huang is close to Donald Trump, so it’s possible that Alice Huang could have gained glimpses into US AI policy as it was being formed, into Trump’s thinking on AI, or into Nvidia’s company strategy. The earliest picture of them together is at an after-party following a tech trade show in Taipei, taken in 2024. But without seeing the evidence, all this is speculation.

What does this reveal about Chinese espionage?.

Diungkapkan bahwa the us has been historically cautious about allowing ai chips to end up in chinese hands. In 2022, Joe Biden’s administration introduced the Chips and Science Act, which restricted the sale of US chips in China, banning the export of most Nvidia chips. “They’ve been doing this for decades. And now it’s no longer engines they’re interested in, but AI. “The Chinese have a very strong pedigree for industrial espionage and copying other nations’ technologies,” Steve Tsang, the director of the SOAS China Institute, tells me. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, both the us and china have an interest in gathering intelligence about each other’s ai firms. What’s more remarkable is the possibility that the Chinese spy agency, the MSS, could have recruited Alice Huang as a “honeytrap” to ensnare Jensen Huang – a method fraught with risk, which seems more reminiscent of 1970s spy fiction than contemporary counterintelligence (China, for its part, has rejected claims that Alice Huang was a spy).

“The facts clearly aren’t established, but it seems more likely that if Alice Huang was working for Beijing, the MSS would have recruited her after they became aware of her relationship with Huang, not before,” Nigel Inkster, the former director of operations and intelligence for the British Secret Intelligence Service, tells me.

Sebagaimana diketahui, china has built a large intelligence gathering operation: the mss is now bigger than the cia, and various national security laws mean that chinese nationals can be required to provide assistance to the chinese state. So can visiting academics. “Business delegations travelling abroad can be tasked with gathering information. “You have a lot of people who can be co-opted into intelligence gathering, all of whom can be tasked with different requirements,” Inkster says. ”.

“The big question, to my mind, is whether the Chinese intelligence agencies have actually been willing to deliver unwelcome information to the party leadership,” Inkster adds.

Sebagaimana diketahui, wading through streams and bushes to the plane wreckage, where a tourist posed for pictures. Credit.

Reporting from Bougainville, Papua New Guinea.

Halfway through the morning, I’m being tossed around like a popcorn kernel in the back of a troop carrier playing an eclectic medley of Backstreet Boys and Papua New Guinean jams.

Berdasarkan laporan, we’re traveling along what feels more like a collection of loose rocks, arranged to be roughly vehicle width, than a road. I’ve lost count of the number of river crossings, including one where the water lapped a few inches from the car’s windows. And this is during a dry spell.

Our caravan is headed for an unlikely tourist destination deep in the jungle on Bougainville Island, an autonomous region of Papua New Guinea in the Solomon Sea.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the piecemeal remnants of a mitsubishi g4m1 — betty, as the planes were code-named by the allies in world war ii — have remained for some 80 years at the crash site of japanese navy adm. Isoroku Yamamoto. This is the spot where Admiral Yamamoto, mastermind of the Pearl Harbor attack, archvillain to Americans in the war, a respected and memorialized figure to the Japanese, met his end in 1943.

Sebagaimana diketahui, bougainville was occupied by the japanese in early 1942, in the months after pearl harbor, as the imperial navy pushed into the south pacific, with admiral yamamoto at the helm. In April 1943, Allied forces intercepted and deciphered Japanese communication on the admiral’s travels, and American P-38 Lightning fighters gunned down his plane over southern Bougainville, a feat the Americans triumphantly dubbed Operation Vengeance.

In February, Kenya’s intelligence services reported that more than 1,000 Kenyans had been lured to fight for Russia.

A growing number of people from African countries – including Kenya, Uganda and South Africa – and elsewhere have been lured to the frontline as Russia seeks help to sustain its more than four-year war after invading Ukraine in February 2022.

The posts promised lucrative jobs in logistics, border security and defence construction, but after the applicants travelled to Russia they were directed to sign contracts to serve as mercenaries, with some deployed to conflict zones, police said.

The ‘I Want to Live’ governmental initiative was established in September 2022 by the coordination headquarters for Prisoners of War with support from Ukraine defence ministry and defence intelligence (HUR).

Indonesia's vice-president resigns amid signs ruling alliance is fraying

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmvgxgz87qqro?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

President Prabowo (left) said he was sorry to lose Gibran Rakabuming Raka (right), who has been mired in a growing controversy over his high school credentials.

Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka tendered his resignation to parliament on Thursday, triggering the process of finding his replacement amid growing turmoil for the government.

Gibran had been facing impeachment calls after a Supreme Court ruling that a high-school document used during his 2024 election campaign was invalid.

His departure comes amid a faltering political alliance between his father, ex-president Joko Widodo, and the incumbent President Prabowo Subianto.

Sebagaimana diketahui, standing alongside gibran, prabowo told reporters he had accepted his resignation with "a heavy heart". Upper house lawmakers will have 60 days to fill the vacancy from two candidates nominated by the president.

"[Gibran] has demonstrated a chivalrous attitude, a strong sense of responsibility, and the qualities of a statesman," Prabowo said, adding that the resignation was "for the benefit of the nation, the state, and the people of Indonesia".

Sebagaimana diketahui, "he certainly believes that he completed his education through a proper and structured process. However, we must understand that educational systems abroad differ from those in Indonesia," the president said.

Gibran has long faced controversy over whether his high school qualifications met legal requirements to run for office.

Having studied in Singapore and Australia, he had used an Indonesian equivalence certificate to demonstrate his educational credentials.

Indonesian law requires vice-presidents to have completed senior secondary school or its equivalent, but the Supreme Court found no evidence to prove Gibran had graduated.

"No evidence was found to show Gibran had a foreign diploma or certificate that could serve as the basis for equivalency with a senior high school or equivalent qualification," it said.

It also considered a Constitutional Court ruling from earlier in October which came to the same conclusion.

The Supreme Court ruling prompted more than 100 lawmakers to support a parliamentary initiative that could have paved the way for proceedings to impeach Gibran.

Gibran previously argued that undertaking university education was sufficient proof that he had completed senior high school.

On Tuesday, he asked for the chance to challenge the ruling and be given the opportunity to prove the legitimacy of his education credentials, State Secretariat Prasetyo Hadi said.

Gibran's ascension to Prabowo's ticket in the 2024 election was part of an alliance formed between his father, outgoing president Joko Widodo - known as Jokowi - and Prabowo, his erstwhile bitter rival.

Gibran was 36 at the time, and only became eligible for candidacy after a controversial ruling by the Constitutional Court, which exempted him from the minimum age requirement of 40.

But tensions between Jokowi and Prabowo appear to have flared.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, since taking the presidency, prabowo has shown little interest in pushing ahead with jokowi's legacy project: the construction of nusantara, a new capital. Instead, he has focused much of the state's resources on his own flagship programme to provide free school meals across the country.

In a series of personnel reshuffles over the past year, Prabowo has also shifted many Jokowi loyalists into new roles, including long-serving finance minister Sri Mulyani Indrawati.

Last week, authorities arrested several senior officials, including presidential chief of staff Listyo Sigit Prabowo - no relation to Prabowo - on suspicions of wiretapping the president.

Prabowo sacked Listyo a day later, in what many pointed to as a sign of a crumbling alliance: Listyo, who formerly served as the national police chief, is widely considered a long-time ally of Jokowi.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, within the government, allegiances seem to be shifting. On Monday, three members of Prabowo's cabinet collectively resigned from the party led by Kaesang Pangarep, Jokowi's youngest son, citing their desire to focus on their duties in Prabowo's administration.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but neither man has confirmed the rift. Speaking to reporters on Thursday, Jokowi said he still supported Prabowo's leadership.

Jokowi also said Gibran's resignation was part of "political dynamics" and he had told his son "the position was temporary".

Berdasarkan laporan, all this is unfolding at a particularly turbulent period in prabowo's presidency. The free school meals programme is struggling for funding, parts of Indonesia have recently battled the country's worst wildfires in a decade, and the national stock market faces crisis amid allegations of widespread market manipulation.

Across the country, students and activists have staged demonstrations to protest against the government's handling of a range of issues, including the environmental crisis and corruption.

#94. Microsoft scrambles to fix global outage affecting Teams and Outlook

📅 13 Nov 2026

Microsoft scrambles to fix global outage affecting Teams and Outlook

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/13/microsoft-outage-outlook-teams-word-excel-reports

Tech company ‘seeing positive results’ with efforts and says no indication problem was caused by cyber-attack.

Tell us: have you been affected by the Microsoft outage?.

Microsoft is scrambling to fix an outage of some of its systems that has caused huge disruption to users, organisations and businesses across the globe.

The tech company said it was “seeing positive results” in its efforts to improve capacity to enable more users to get back on its systems, after a global outage affected millions of users for more than 12 hours on Thursday and Friday.

In an update shortly after 7am GMT, it said: “We’re seeing positive results for server stability after applying an upstream authentication/routing configuration component patch to a portion of our infrastructure.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we’ll continue to monitor its progress and are working to expand it to servers supporting active regions coming online. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the issue appears patchy, with some but not all users reporting problems with services including microsoft teams and outlook email. More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, and more than 90% of Fortune 500 companies use Copilot, Microsoft’s AI chatbot, according to the company.

Microsoft said that there were no indications that the outage was caused by a cyber-attack.

Berdasarkan laporan, earlier, the company had said it was only seeing “marginal success” from its efforts to bring its systems fully back online. It had said that a portion of its infrastructure was “experiencing elevated load” – which was “likely contributing to the connectivity errors”.

The company determined a number of servers were “unexpectedly unavailable” because of a problem that caused them to fail during automated checks.

It earlier warned that services that have restarted can become unresponsive again once they receive traffic.

“Once mitigated, we will provide full details of the root cause, defence-in-depth repair items, and more within a post-incident report,” Microsoft said.

Berdasarkan laporan, the outage website down detector showed an increase in microsoft 365 problems at about 6pm gmt on thursday, with nearly 130,000 reports of problems in 74 countries affecting access to word, excel, powerpoint, outlook and teams as well as enterprise services such as sharepoint and onedrive. AI assistant Copilot was also affected.

Microsoft has suggested the outage may have been caused by problems with the settings applied to servers responsible for keeping Microsoft 365 up and running.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, microsoft’s executive vice-president of copilot, charles lamanna, posted on x that the company would share more information when it became available. “We regret that today’s outages caused disruptions for our customers, and we are working to address the issue,” he said.

The Microsoft outage also hit connectors used by ⁠OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s AI ⁠services.

Sebagaimana diketahui, openai said it was investigating an issue with microsoft connectors in which new connections may be broken and tools were not working as ⁠expected. Anthropic said it had identified an issue with an upstream provider ​affecting its Microsoft 365 ​connector.

The UK government said it was “working closely” with Microsoft to assess any impact on government services, adding that there were “robust contingency plans in place to minimise disruption”.

The outage has affected businesses and organisations across the world that use Microsoft products.

Several UK police forces have urged people not to try to report crimes online and to phone them in instead.

Berdasarkan laporan, some schools in the uk have notified parents that services such as email and teams are down, and that reporting attendance or absence issues has to be done via phone. A primary school in Salisbury reassured parents that, while school communications have been disrupted, classes will not be affected.

An NHS provider to London, Milton Keynes and Surrey said email was disrupted and apologised for the inconvenience.

The Indian airlines IndiGo and Akasa Air said their email support services were affected, and Taiwanese security firms, life insurers and investment trust companies said fund management services had been disrupted.

Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning.

In financial markets some portfolio managers have been unable to check emails, making it hard to access on some trading platforms.

In Japan, the shipping company Sagawa Express said it was unable to accept online reservations for some of its services at airports and train stations while Taisho, a major pharmaceutical company, said it was having to handle orders by phone.

In Australia experts estimate the outage will cost its economy billions of dollars.

Microsoft last month reported an ​outage of its Azure cloud platform that affected a ​suite of productivity software ‌and a range ​of industries worldwide.

Mark Gregory, an associate professor in the School of Engineering at RMIT University, said the outage appears to be affecting the network layer in Microsoft’s systems, and was potentially similar to the configuration issue that brought down Optus’s network in 2023.

He said when some of the servers have configuration issues, it means customers are forced to share a smaller pool of servers to access the cloud services.

Diungkapkan bahwa “if you lose part of that pool, then all of the users are trying to access the remaining servers, and that overloads them. And then they go down.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “and so you end up with a cascading problem. Then it takes time to find the underlying problem, in this case, a misconfiguration in the network layer. ”.

Gregory said it showed companies should invest more in testing environments for configuration changes before deployment in the live network, and said businesses reliant on cloud services such as Microsoft 365 should have backup options.

“From a global perspective, there is someone somewhere that’s been badly affected by this and you end up with lost productivity,” he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “they’re being left high and dry now … it then becomes important to have an alternative. ”.

Earlier, the company said it had “successfully restored” problems related to Microsoft Teams in North America, although some users continued to report connectivity issues.

Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report.

#97. Famed ship SS United States deliberately sunk off Florida coast to become a reef

📅 12 Nov 2026

Famed ship SS United States deliberately sunk off Florida coast to become a reef

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c3x298n87rn2o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Watch: Moment historic ship sinks off the coast of Florida.

A ship that was once the fastest in the world and is longer than the Titanic has intentionally been sunk off the coast of Florida, turning into the world's largest artificial ocean reef.

The SS United States spent nearly 30 years docked in Philadelphia before it was moved to Florida, where it will become a home for sealife and an underwater attraction for marine enthusiasts.

Activists unsuccessfully fought for the historic liner - which crossed the Atlantic Ocean hundreds of times - to be preserved as a museum.

Instead, after being purchased by a Florida county, it was added to the dozens of artificial reefs off the coast, with a land-based museum detailing the ship's history also planned.

Before its retirement, the SS United States was known for carrying royalty and celebrities between the US and Europe, beginning in 1952 and ending in 1969.

Berdasarkan laporan, a young bill clinton, before he was president, used the ship to cross the atlantic. Former presidents Harry Truman, Dwight Eisenhower and John Kennedy also travelled on the vessel.

The ship was moved from Philadelphia to Alabama last year for cleaning and remediation work.

On Monday, it took its final journey from Alabama to the coast of Destin, Florida, where it was sunk on Wednesday in a precision operation without explosives.

This archival video shows the SS United States in 2025 as it starts its move to Florida on its way to become the world's largest artificial reef.

Stars including Marlon Brando, Coco Chanel, Duke Ellington, Salvador Dali, Walt Disney, Judy Garland and Cary Grant also boarded the ship during its sailing lifetime.

Before its purchase by the municipal Florida government, a number of proposals that would have seen the ship live a second life as a museum or a floating hotel failed.

Instead, it sat at various docks with various owners as legal battles played out.

The SS United States Conservancy group repeatedly attempted to keep the ship above water, but was unsuccessful.

Conservancy President Susan Gibbs - whose grandfather helped design the liner - said she was glad that the story of the SS United States would live on.

"[The ship] has always been this unabashedly American symbol that brings so many people together," Gibbs told CBS News, the BBC's US partner.

#99. A baffling trail from Australia to Singapore: what is Megaspeed, the company implicated in downfall of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang?

📅 13 Nov 2026

A baffling trail from Australia to Singapore: what is Megaspeed, the company implicated in downfall of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang?

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/13/a-baffling-trail-from-australia-to-singapore-what-is-megaspeed-the-company-implicated-in-downfall-of-nvidias-jensen-huang

Few solid clues have emerged as to the true nature of Megaspeed, whose former director Alice Huang has been accused of being a Chinese spy.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

From washing dishes at Denny’s to rockstar of AI: the rise and fall of Jensen Huang.

A lottery retailer in rural Australia, a dilapidated storefront in Kuala Lumpur, and a near-empty office in Singapore: the global facades of Megaspeed International, the company linked to the downfall of Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, form a puzzling corporate picture.

The company, which is registered in Singapore, has registered affiliates across the US, Asia and Australia, but individuals at its offices say they know nothing about the cloud computing firm at the centre of a global spy scandal.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on friday huang resigned as chief executive of the chip manufacturer nvidia after reports of extramarital affairs with an alleged chinese spy and two company employees. US intelligence agencies believe Huang had been targeted by Alice Huang (no relation), the former director of Megaspeed International.

US officials believe Huang was acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, passing commercial information to Beijing, the New York Times has reported.

On Thursday, Singaporean authorities said Alice Huang had been barred from re-entering the city state after a 2025 investigation into the company.

Singapore police said last October they were investigating Megaspeed over “suspected breaches of our domestic laws” after a US senator requested the commerce department investigate whether the firm had diverted Nvidia chips.

Berdasarkan laporan, the ministry of home affairs said this week it had held alice huang’s passport from june 2025 until february over “potential false declarations” related to megaspeed. Eventually, she was released with a stern warning.

Earlier this week, authorities in Taiwan said she had also been barred from re-entering there.

On Friday Malaysia said it was investigating a subsidiary of Megaspeed International over the possible diversion of advanced AI chips to other countries.

Across the region, Megaspeed’s activities remain obscure.

In Sydney, no signage, mailbox or physical presence suggests the company at the epicentre of one of the biggest stories in the world is located on the 10th floor of an office building in the city centre.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “do you have an appointment?” a receptionist asked when the guardian visted the office, home to numerous businesses. It hummed with activity but no one had heard of Megaspeed Australia or its listed director, 29-year-old Kai Kang.

Berdasarkan laporan, megaspeed international filed papers in the us state of delaware ⁠and with the australian securities and investments commission (asic), showing the affiliates were created in 2024. Both filings list the Shanghai-born Kang as the sole company officer, either as ​director or president.

The Australian ‌filing also lists the Singapore-based parent as ‌the company’s stockholder.

Reuters ‌visited the home address provided on the filings for the affiliates – a small store, a news agency and lottery retailer, in Seymour, Victoria, about an hour’s drive north of Melbourne.

Berdasarkan laporan, a woman, who identified herself as kang’s mother, said she had run the business for about 16 years. She said Kang was based in Shanghai and did not know anything about the Singaporean company.

“He doesn’t have any business here,” she said, adding that Kang had completed his master’s degree at Shanghai University.

He had visited his parents most recently in August and September, she said.

She said she knew about Nvidia and Megaspeed but her son had nothing to do with the company in Singapore.

It is not the only perplexing finding that journalists have encountered when trying to track down representatives of Megaspeed, which in the past three years has been one of Nvidia’s biggest foreign customers, purchasing nearly $5bn in AI chips and advanced hardware.

The Straits Times reported that Swiftdata, the little-known company that owns Megaspeed, had a registered business address in Singapore, but an interior design firm said it had occupied the premises for more than four years.

Last year the New York Times visited Megaspeed’s Singapore headquarters, located in the central business district, but found only two employees present.

Berdasarkan laporan, and in neighbouring malaysia, the times found that one of megaspeed’s offices was a dilapidated storefront in the capital. Another was located in a shopping mall. When one employee emerged in the mall, she was asked what the company did.

Kang is also registered as a director in Megaspeed’s Malaysian, Indonesian and Thai units.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, kang has not been accused of any wrongdoing. Attempts to contact him were unsuccessful.

In Australia, a former intelligence officer said they expected Australian security agencies would have sought briefings from overseas counterparts about Megaspeed or undertaken their own assessments of the local subsidiary this week.

Michael Shoebridge, the director of the security thinktank Strategic Analysis Australia and a former deputy of the Australian Signals Directorate and the Defence Intelligence Organisation (Asio), said key details about Megaspeed’s relationship with Chinese intelligence remained unclear.

He suggested it would be “credible” to assess the company as a “front for Chinese intelligence” but nothing was certain.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the chinese government has flatly rejected any claims alice huang was a spy. A foreign ministry spokesperson, Guo Jiakun, said earlier this week the allegations were “unsubstantiated” and “nothing but smears against China”.

Shoebridge said Megaspeed’s Australian operation could be a legitimate business or designed to make the Singapore-based parent company “look credible” by having overseas affiliates.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, asio declined to comment when asked if it was examining megaspeed australia. The office of the Australian home affairs minister, Tony Burke, also declined to comment.

The acting prime minister, Richard Marles, was asked on ABC TV this week whether there had been discussions inside government “about some of the potential spying that could be taking place within Australian companies”.

Diungkapkan bahwa on abc radio, marles, speaking generally, said: “we are living in a world where there is more espionage than there has been for a long time. A lot of that is particularly around emerging technologies. ”.

The federal opposition said any potential foreign interference “must be taken seriously”.

An email to the Victorian newsagent and messages to its Facebook page requesting comment went unanswered on Thursday.

Diungkapkan bahwa asic documents show kang was born in 1996 in shanghai and has been listed as megaspeed australia’s director since the company was registered. They reveal Megaspeed International owns all 10,000 shares of Megaspeed Australia’s stocks, for which it paid $1m.

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/11/world/middleeast/us-blockade-iran-taskforce-iron-gate.html

Berdasarkan laporan, washington wants to intensify its economic pressure campaign on iran by closing its land borders. Neighboring states, fearing economic fallout, are pushing back.

By Erika SolomonEric Schmitt and Tyler Pager.

Diungkapkan bahwa the first step in the united states’ campaign to economically strangle iran was a naval blockade of its ports, cutting off iranian trade by sea. Next came a raft of new sanctions, grounding much of the country’s air transport network.

Berdasarkan laporan, now, the united states is going after iran’s last economic artery: its land routes. Only there, Washington has hit upon a problem.

Berdasarkan laporan, for weeks, u. officials have tried — and failed — to diplomatically pressure Iran’s neighbors into shuttering their border crossings, according to three Iraqi officials and one U. S. S. official with knowledge of the talks, who requested anonymity to speak candidly.

Berdasarkan laporan, those neighboring states, primarily turkey, iraq and pakistan, are increasingly wary and disgruntled by u. S. policies they say could hurt them as much as Tehran.

#102. Kidnapper, 74, escapes from house arrest in Argentina by abseiling from balcony

📅 11 Nov 2026

Kidnapper, 74, escapes from house arrest in Argentina by abseiling from balcony

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c933gn6710lyo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Leonardo Bertulazzi was first arrested in Buenos Aires in 2002.

A 74-year-old Italian man who was found guilty of a kidnapping carried out by a far-left militant group in the 1970s has escaped while under house arrest in Argentina and is on the run.

Leonardo Bertulazzi used a harness to abseil down from a fifth-floor balcony in the capital, Buenos Aires.

His escape was not immediately registered because he had tampered with his electronic ankle monitor so that it continued to transmit body temperature measurements even after he had prised it open and absconded.

Bertulazzi already spent decades as a fugitive after he was sentenced in absentia in Italy for the 1977 kidnapping of Italian naval engineer Pietro Costa.

He was awaiting extradition to Italy and was being monitored by the Argentine ministry of security through an ankle tag which registers the wearer's body temperature and movements.

Officials said that they had become suspicious when they noticed that the tag had remained stationary.

When they entered the fifth-floor apartment in the centre of Buenos Aires, Bertulazzi was gone, but the ankle monitor remained.

Wary of Bertulazzi's past with the Marxist guerilla group the Red Brigades and his bomb-making skills, police called in explosives experts in case it had been rigged to detonate, according to Argentine newspaper ClarÃ­n.

However, the experts found that while Bertulazzi had tampered with the device, he had done so to prevent the alarm from sounding once he removed it.

Italian media say that his extradition to Italy had been imminent after his last appeal was rejected.

Bertulazzi was first arrested after using a false passport to cross into Argentina from neighbouring Chile in 2002.

However, he was granted refugee status in 2004 and lived freely in the South American country until his re-arrest in 2024, when the current right-wing president, Javier Milei, took office.

Milei's government said at the time that "Bertulazzi is responsible for crimes that undermined democratic values and the lives of many victims".

He was a member of the Red Brigades, which kidnapped and killed a number of state officials in the 1970s and '80s.

Bertulazzi was part of the Red Brigades' Genoa section that kidnapped Pietro Costa on the street and then held him for 81 days before receiving a big ransom.

The money it made from the kidnapping was then used to buy a flat in Rome, which was used in 1978 for the Red Brigades' most notorious crime, the kidnap and murder of Italian former Prime Minister, Aldo Moro.

Sebagaimana diketahui, moro was abducted when his car was ambushed on the way to the opening of parliament. He was held in the flat for 54 days before he was shot and his body abandoned in the boot of a Renault car in the centre of Rome.

Greens say they will not direct preferences to Labor in 15 seats after party’s ‘unforgivable’ decision earlier in week.

Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast.

The Greens have retaliated against Labor’s decision to run an open ticket in a key inner-city seat by refusing to direct preferences to the party in 15 electorates across the state at this month’s Victorian election.

The move has sparked a war of words between the two parties, with each accusing the other of striking a “dodgy deal” that could help the Liberals and One Nation get elected on 28 November.

On Friday, the Greens confirmed they would only be directing voters to number the Greens one and One Nation last across 15 electorates.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the decision follows labor’s decision on tuesday to run an open ticket in the inner melbourne seat of prahran, where the greens had been counting on labor preferences to win it back. It has been held by the Liberals on a tiny 1. 3% margin – after the Greens lost it at a byelection in 2025.

At the time, the Victorian Greens leader, Ellen Sandell, told Guardian Australia that Labor’s “unforgivable” decision could hand the upcoming election to a Liberal-One Nation coalition.

A Labor spokesperson turned the accusation back on the Greens on Friday, mirroring Sandell’s language.

“In one of the most consequential elections in Victoria’s history – the Greens have done a dodgy deal to help elect a Liberal-One Nation government,” the spokesperson said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “this is unforgivable and victorians won’t forget it’s ellen sandell and the greens to blame when jess wilson cuts our hospitals and schools – and one nation winds back our nation leading reforms on women’s rights and treaty. ”.

The Greens responded by accusing Labor of “lying to Victorian voters”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “the greens will be putting one nation last in every single electorate across victoria,” their spokesperson said. “We always encourage people to vote in line with their values.

Diungkapkan bahwa “after months of scaremongering about a liberal-one nation government, it is labor who have done a dodgy backroom deal with the liberals that could help elect one. ”.

The 15 electorates where the Greens will issue these how-to-vote cards are: Albert Park, Ashwood, Bellarine, Bendigo East, Bendigo West, Essendon, Euroa, Gippsland East, Mildura, Mornington, Point Cook, Polwarth, South Barwon, Tarneit and Werribee.

Labor fears the decision will particularly hurt their chances in Albert Park, Ashwood, Bellarine, South Barwon and the two Bendigo seats vacated by former premier Jacinta Allan and speaker Maree Edwards.

Our political team brings you up to speed on the stories that really matter and what they mean for you.

The Coalition is quietly confident it is improving its chances of fending off One Nation and snatching seats from Labor.

However, Tony Barry, the Liberal strategist turned pollster with Redbridge and co-host of Guardian Australia’s Back to Back Barries podcast, said most Greens voters don’t closely follow their party’s how-to-vote cards.

“Historical preference flows from past state and federal elections shows about 85% of exhausted Greens votes flow to Labor and about 15% leakage to the Coalition, and that rarely changes regardless of the particular circumstances,” Barry said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but he said in essendon, where labor candidate kat theodosis is contesting the seat following danny pearson’s retirement, in a complex race involving the liberals, one nation and three independents candidates, it “might be enough to flip the seat to the liberals. ”.

Meanwhile, the conservative Family First party is directing its preferences to Labor candidates affiliated with the Shop, Distributive and Allied Employees’ Association (SDA), placing them second on their how-to-vote cards.

The cards feature an image of a baby next to the Labor candidate name with claims they have a “pro-life voting record”.

It prompted Pasoce Vale MP Anthony Cianflone, who is in a tight race against the Greens’ Angelica Panopoulos, to post a statement on social media saying he supported “women’s right to make their own decisions about their bodies and healthcare”.

“That’s why I have supported the Victorian Labor government’s reforms protecting these rights,” Cianflone said.

Family First have also preferenced Matthew Guy last in his safe Liberal seat of Bulleen.

Berdasarkan laporan, the family first state leader, moira deeming, was disendorsed as a liberal candidate after alleging guy had placed her in a headlock earlier this year. Deeming later conceded she misunderstood the technical meaning of “headlock”.

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cwz0k79pr8z2o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

These children had to leave their primary school in Rome as a result of one of the threats sent on Wednesday.

Some 6,300 schools across Italy and more than 700 in Scotland and Northern Ireland have received bomb threats, according to local authorities.

In Italy a number of buildings were evacuated as a precaution but Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said checks so far had not indicated any evidence of "concrete danger".

"These reports appear rather linked to a strategy intended to cause alarm and concern," she said on Facebook.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, scotland's education secretary mairi mcallan said there was no risk to the public and specialist cyber-crime officers were working to identify the source of the messages. In Northern Ireland education officials told schools to remain open unless otherwise advised by police.

It is unclear whether the incidents are connected.

"As a parent and as a constituency MSP I understand just how concerning this will be for parents, for pupils, for carers and for school staff," McAllan said.

Diungkapkan bahwa scottish police had earlier said that the warnings were "immediately assessed" as hoaxes. However some local authorities confirmed that some schools had been evacuated.

"Our advice is that there is no requirement to evacuate schools or keep children away from education based solely on the content of the emails," Police Scotland said.

Italian officials said a single email appeared to have been sent on Wednesday to the inboxes of 6,300 out of a total of 7,476 state schools, and private schools were unaffected.

The message, said to be from a certain "Mikhail Andropov, leader of Vilayat di Misoginistan", caused alarm in many schools.

The BBC has seen the email sent to Scottish schools which appeared to have similar wording, and also referenced the name Mikhail Andropov, although as leader of a "Red Owl" project.

Italy's Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara said the incidents involving Italian schools were probably a "cyber-attack, not a genuine risk", adding that there appeared to be a clear strategy behind the rash of threats in across Europe targeting flights, supermarkets and even hospitals.

Italian airports along with airlines elsewhere in Europe were hit by a series of bomb hoaxes last week that prompted a series of scares, evacuations and widespread disruption.

Although a number of threats were claimed by an extremist misogynistic group, it later denied any link to the false warnings.

No risk to public from hoax school bomb threats, says government minister.

Police treating threatening email sent to more than 300 schools as 'hoax'.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on wednesday one milan headteacher, anna bertato, told italian media she had checked the email address of the sender online: "it was already classified as spam by a student at a university in taiwan. ".

Another Milan headteacher, Massimo Nunzio Barrella, told Adnkronos news agency that he had immediately realised the email was spam when it arrived in his inbox at 08:59 and he decided not to evacuate his school and reassured parents who phoned in.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the text seemed almost comical," said barrella, "it was like a message from martians: 'we have come to annihilate you. ' I even had a bit of a laugh. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, although many schools were initially evacuated on wednesday, the alarm was quickly lifted, and pupils were allowed to return to class. Some parents decided to take their children home for the day, but the majority of schools in Milan did not send their pupils home.

Some 280 school head teachers had already received threats in recent days, according to Italian reports.

In a statement, the head of the central Umbria region Stefania Proietti said "checks conducted so far in Umbrian schools have proved negative, and law enforcement is working rapidly and carefully to verify each report".

#109. ‘If I wanted to plan a murder’: Beau Lamarre-Condon tells court what he would have done

‘If I wanted to plan a murder’: Beau Lamarre-Condon tells court what he would have done

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/13/beau-lamarre-condon-trial-sim-card-pseudonym-ntwnfb

Former police officer tells court ‘it was never a plan to murder anybody’ as prosecution repeatedly suggests to him he planned to kill Jesse Baird.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

Beau Lamarre-Condon has told a Sydney court he never planned to murder anybody and if he did, he reiterated he would use stolen vehicles and a gun not linked to him.

Diungkapkan bahwa but the prosecutor responded: “no one’s saying it was a good plan, that’s why you’re sitting here. ”.

The former police officer is accused of fatally shooting Jesse Baird and his new partner, Luke Davies, with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024.

He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.

Sat in the witness box for the seventh day, Lamarre-Condon was asked about driving his mother to pick up a hire car under her name on the evening before the alleged murders.

As part of his cross-examination, crown prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC repeatedly suggested to Lamarre-Condon that he was planning to murder Baird.

Berdasarkan laporan, but the accused told the new south wales supreme court on friday: “it was never a plan to murder anybody. ”.

“You wouldn’t bring a vehicle linked to your mum for a murder,” Lamarre-Condon told the jury.

Diungkapkan bahwa “if i wanted to a plan a murder, i would have two stolen vehicles ready to go; i would have a gun that’s not linked to me. I know exactly how to do it. I work with youth gangs. ”.

Hatfield told Lamarre-Condon: “No one’s saying it was a good plan, that’s why you’re sitting here, isn’t it?”.

The former officer maintained he and his mother spoke in the car about his suicidal ideation, and he had turned off his phone because he did not want to talk about work or personal things in the vicinity of the device.

On Friday afternoon, Hatfield began questioning Lamarre-Condon about the disposal of the bodies and the clean up of the alleged scene of the crime.

He suggested to the accused that he began going through Baird’s phone on the afternoon of the shootings and using it to send messages.

“This is where there’s lots of times where there were blackouts,” Lamarre-Condon told the court.

He agreed the messages were sent by him but could not give an accurate recollection of what he did.

A day later, he met up with a friend at a Sushi Train restaurant, where they spoke about disposing the bodies, Lamarre-Condon told the court.

The other man was young and was hoping to become a police officer, the jury heard.

Lamarre-Condon claims the friend suggested sinking the bodies with concrete, which was questioned by Hatfield.

“You’re taking advice from this young, immature guy about what do to with the bodies … is that seriously your evidence?” the prosecutor asked.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “you won’t take responsibility for the decision of how you treated the bodies, you want to blame [your friends]. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, lamarre-condon responded: “he gave me the suggestion, i’m not saying he put all the ideas in my head. ”.

The prosecutor said it was “quite an extreme thing to be taking two men’s bodies and treat them the way you did” and the former police officer agreed his conduct was “not OK”.

Berdasarkan laporan, but hatfield replied: “i didn’t ask whether it’s ok. It’s beyond argument it’s not right. ”.

“It’s extraordinary conduct that was inconsistent with manslaughter and inconsistent with any accidental killing,” he told the court.

Lamarre-Condon admitted that on the night of 20 February 2024, he activated Baird’s phone near the Paddington home and began responding to the dead man’s notifications and sending messages.

The crown prosecutor suggested he was thinking about how the evidence from his phone would look and was “thinking strategically”.

Lamarre-Condon said it was “common sense”.

Hatfield asked: “Common sense when you’re carrying out a murder, is that right?”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the accused responded: “i didn’t carry out murder; i’m guilty of manslaughter. ”.

Earlier on Friday, Lamarre-Condon was asked about buying a sim card under the name “Bob Ballard” on 15 January 2024, about a month before the shootings.

He told the jury in his double murder trial it had “nothing to do with Jesse Baird”.

He was attempting to compile statements about “bullying from a certain sergeant” but was worried about speaking publicly on the issue, Lamarre-Condon said.

“I was wanting to go and compile all these statements and go to the media,” he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i didn’t want to communicate at all from my phone because you can become a target … there would be repercussions. ”.

Under cross-examination by Hatfield, Lamarre-Condon agreed he was using the new sim card to contact former and current officers.

Berdasarkan laporan, but asked why his phone records showed he only contacted one police officer on this sim, lamarre-condon said it only revealed his normal phone calls, telling the court: “you can’t see what i did on signal. ”.

The prosecutor said he could have used the encrypted messaging app Signal on his normal phone, but Lamarre-Condon claimed police could make him unlock his own device and view his Signal records if he was investigated for talking to the media.

Hatfield also questioned why Lamarre-Condon had Davies’s contact details on his phone.

The former officer claimed Davies’s details were on his Instagram.

“I went and blocked numerous Instagram [accounts] from my own Instagram because of this incident,” he said, referring to the shootings.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i even blocked jesse’s family members from my account. I didn’t want any of that. ”.

He deactivated his social media accounts soon after.

The trial before Justice Natalie Adams continues.
