Watch: County Sheriff describes how buried baby was found.

An 11-month-old baby has been rescued in South Carolina after officials say he was buried alive in a crate by his father.

Diungkapkan bahwa koah sharpe had been missing since monday when he was taken by his father, michael comer, 25, according to the lexington county sheriff's department. Comer was arrested on a burglary charge on Monday evening but his son was not with him.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the baby was found on tuesday "buried alive" and "clinging to life" not far from his father's house, lexington county sheriff jay koon said at a news conference. It is thought he had been there for 24 hours.

The child is now in hospital receiving care, Koon said, adding he was hopeful he would make a full recovery.

Police are still deciding what further charges to bring against the father.

The search for baby Koah began on Monday after his father took him from his mother's house.

Comer's mother was watching the child and had left her son alone with him briefly, Koon said, when he left abruptly with Koah.

Officials allege the baby's father buried him alive in a dog crate.

Berdasarkan laporan, comer was seen travelling to multiple locations without the baby and was later arrested in lexington county without koah. A search party of 100 police and fire department officials were then sent to search for the child, the sheriff said.

He added that when they asked Comer where his son was, he "did not have much to say" about his whereabouts.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, koon said that rescuers searched the woods near comer's house and saw some "freshly disturbed dirt". As they began to dig, they heard a baby crying - something the sheriff described as "the most joyful sound you ever heard".

Diungkapkan bahwa "the race was on. Everybody was getting down there trying to get him out," Koon added.

He said the crate was wrapped in a towel that probably provided enough air for Koah to survive for as long as he did, while the cold weather kept him from getting too hot.

Berdasarkan laporan, "the crate was, probably, i'm guessing about a two-foot [61cm] by two-foot dog crate. So, I think, once that crate hit the ground, he was probably up at least a foot from the top of that crate to the top of the ground," Koon explained.

Diungkapkan bahwa of the parents' relationship, the sheriff said there were "obviously some issues". Comer had previously pleaded guilty to domestic violence charges, court records show.

Sebagaimana diketahui, comer's mother, patricia comer, told nbc news that koah's mother had full custody of him but allowed her to supervise while her son watched him. She said her son had watched the baby before unsupervised without any problems.

"Honestly, I'm his mother, and I never expected this from him," Patricia Comer said.

#113. Minister’s office said contractor should handle CFMEU or lose work in Victoria, Big Build inquiry hears

📅 13 Nov 2026

Minister’s office said contractor should handle CFMEU or lose work in Victoria, Big Build inquiry hears

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/13/big-build-royal-commission-vida-construction-workers-fearful-cfmeu-ntwnfb

Royal commission also hears from construction company employee who says workers were ‘fearful’ of union.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

A major contractor on a troubled Victorian rail project shut down by union officials was warned that the minister’s office felt it would not “have any more work” in the state if it did not resolve the industrial dispute, a royal commission has heard.

The royal commission into the integrity of major public and civil infrastructure construction projects in Victoria heard from a Victorian Infrastructure Delivery Authority (Vida) official for the first time on Friday.

Vida was strongly criticised by counsel assisting the commission, Chris Young KC, on Thursday for its failure to disclose relevant evidence in a timely manner to the investigation.

The commission’s November public hearings, which are set to run until 20 November, are focusing on a 2022 level crossing removal project at Gap Road in Sunbury.

The commission previously heard that Construction, Forestry and Maritime Employees Union (CFMEU) officials shut down the site because of purported safety concerns, only for them to allow it to continue after two of their own health and safety representatives were appointed, and the project changed its traffic and labour hire companies to CFMEU-aligned firms.

Peter Wilkinson, a former Vida official who is now the executive general manager of the Suburban Rail Loop authority and a civil engineer, said that at the height of an industrial dispute at Gap Road he spoke about the need for work to resume on the project with Evan Tattersall, his manager at Vida.

He said Tattersall told him on either 6 or 7 June 2022 that he had discussed the issue with the minister’s office, and Wilkinson assumed that meant the office of the then-minister for transport infrastructure, Jacinta Allan.

Tattersall told him, Wilkinson said, “that if they can’t handle the industrial [relations] in Victoria, they can’t have any more work”.

Tattersall was referring to the contractors on the site, John Holland and CPB Constructions, Wilkinson said.

Wilkinson said he was aware at the time that the contractors were tendering for the airport rail, another major state government funded infrastructure project, but that he did not know if the minister’s office also knew this.

Wilkinson said Tattersall did not tell him what he should do with the information from the minister’s office, but he passed it on to Joe Aygur, the general manager of the Rail Network Alliance involved in the project’s delivery.

Aygur told the commission about the warning on Tuesday.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when asked by young why no record of his conversation with tattersall existed, wilkinson said “probably one reason is that it was moving very quickly, so it was conversation that we had to keep it moving, rather than there being a need to formally record it. ”.

Wilkinson was also asked about a meeting scheduled in Allan’s parliament house office for 5pm on 7 June 2022 – the day work recommenced at Gap Road.

He was listed as an optional attendee on an online invite for the meeting, but said he could not recall if he attended.

The commission also heard on Friday from Stephen Villella, who worked for CPD Constructions and was the delivery director at the site, about the meeting at the union headquarters that ultimately ended the dispute.

He said it had been “extremely galling” for construction company officials to have to “bend the knee” by meeting with the CFMEU to resolve the matter.

Villella said none of the safety concerns raised by the union were serious enough to force work to stop at the site.

Workers on the project were fearful of the CFMEU and would stay in the lunchroom for long periods once they started to attend.

“They didn’t want to come [to work] at all,” Villella said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “they were fearful of what would happen to them organisationally and individually if they did. ”.

Villella said he disagreed with evidence given early in the week by a former CFMEU organiser Paul Tzimas about those on site choosing not to work, saying they were heavily pressured by union officials.

Villella said that in the meeting with the CFMEU, a union organiser Joe Myles suggested collaborating would assist in winning future tenders such as the Melbourne airport rail project.

He said Myles also suggested he had direct lines to Allan’s office.

Villella said he was not surprised by Myles’ claim about having communication to the ministers office, as he had seen what had happened to the industry over the past 10 years.

Villella said Myles left abruptly in the first half of the about 30 minute meeting, which he said felt like a snub.

But he rejected a suggestion by counsel for Myles that it was not the union official, but rather Tzimas, who raised the list of union demands for the Gap Road project.

After construction managers agreed to the demands, work on the site resumed as normal.

“Amazingly, all our safety issues ceased,” Villella said.

Chris Carr SC, senior counsel assisting the commission, said that after the rebuke issued by Young on Thursday to Vida, he was “happy to report there has been substantial production of highly relevant material overnight”.

He said that production had led to several lines of inquiry, which meant the commission was unlikely to hear from witnesses again until Tuesday.

Workers in a wide range of industries walked off the job to protest rising rents and stagnant wages, which have become central issues in the campaign.

Spanish workers staged a general strike on Wednesday for the first time in 14 years, protesting the rising rents and stagnant wages that have become central issues in the national election to be held this month.

Unions said millions of workers participated in the walkout, while hundreds of thousands of Spaniards joined rallies in Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia and other cities in the evening.

Early on Wednesday, protesters blocked roads in Madrid, set up picket lines outside major factories in Catalonia and disrupted transportation across Spain.

Sebagaimana diketahui, police officers wielding shields and batons forced hundreds of demonstrators away from the gran vía, the central thoroughfare in madrid, which rally goers had blocked. The anger of protesters in the capital was directed largely at “rentistas” — a Spanish term for people who live off rental income.

Diungkapkan bahwa later in the day, during a march through central madrid that drew 120,000 protesters according to the government, demonstrators chanted in a festive mood, “one jump, two jumps, whoever doesn’t jump is a rentista. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, clashes with the police erupted in barcelona, where a group of masked protesters broke away from the crowd after the demonstration ended, according to local news media. The group smashed several shop windows, threw pyrotechnic devices at police officers and tried unsuccessfully to storm an Apple Store, the reports said.

#115. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent relocated after alleged Iranian threats

📅 11 Nov 2026

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent relocated after alleged Iranian threats

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqr7gr0010r2o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

The severity and nature of the threat against Scott Bessent remains unclear.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has been moved from his Washington DC home to a military base after Iran-linked threats to his life, according to US media reports.

CBS, the BBC's US partner, said the relocation came after a photo of Bessent's home was published in the Wall Street Journal.

Bessent has been at the forefront of efforts to isolate Iran economically through sanctions and a wider economic blockade.

While the exact nature of the threats against Bessent remain unclear, US intelligence has warned that Iran has "substantially increased" efforts to target Americans, including US officials.

"After the Wall Street Journal published an article featuring an online photo that allowed the location of the secretary's Georgetown home to be geo-located, security concerns began to increase," a source told CBS.

Georgetown is an affluent part of Washington that is home to a number of government officials and prominent residents.

Those security concerns, the source added, prompted authorities to move Bessent to a military base in the area.

In a statement, a Treasury Department spokesperson said only that Bessent "will not be deterred" by threats and "remains committed" to the US effort to pressure Iran's economy.

The BBC has contacted the White House for comment.

In September, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned that Iran has "substantially increased" efforts to target Americans.

Berdasarkan laporan, the new york times has reported that the iranian effort includes the targeting of current and former us officials. One source told the newspaper this has "reached a more advanced stage".

Other US officials reportedly on Iran's list of potential targets include former Secretary of State Mike Pompeo, former National Security Advisor John Bolton and Mark Milley, the former chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff.

Milley and Bolton's security teams were taken away by the Trump administration shortly after he returned to office last year.

Diungkapkan bahwa bessent is one of a number of administration officials that live on military bases. The White House's new chief of staff, Stephen Miller, was moved to a base in late 2025 - before the conflict with Iran began.

Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio both live on military bases, as did former Attorney General Pam Bondi and former intelligence chief Tulsi Gabbard.

The US and Israel launched an air campaign against Iran in February, killing its leader and prompting the regime in Tehran to retaliate with strikes on US allies across the region and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, through which around a fifth of the world's oil and gas usually travels.

In June, the US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the strait, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated a blockade targeting Iranian ports.

#118. Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing

📅 03 Apr 2023

Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing

Tanggal: 03 Apr 2023 | Sumber: https://www.cnn.com/2023/04/03/politics/chinese-spy-balloon/index.html

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

Berdasarkan laporan, the balloon was able to transmit information back to beijing in real time, the source said, and the us government still does not know for sure whether the chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

Berdasarkan laporan, a us intelligence official told cnn on monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the high altitude balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the united states does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the people’s republic of china. ”.

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, cnn has reached out to the national security council at the white house and the pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the balloon first crossed into us airspace over alaska in late january before passing through canada and down into montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the us to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like malmstrom air force base in montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

Diungkapkan bahwa a senior state department official said in february that, as the balloon floated across the us, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small chinese province of hainan, officials told cnn. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, still, china did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

CNN’s Alex Marquardt contributed to this report.

Leaders meet in Dublin amid search for lead EU negotiator for peace talks with Russia - Europe live

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/13/eu-leaders-negotiations-ukraine-russia-dublin-ai-summit-kushner-witkoff-latest-news-updates

Ukraine and Russia have agreed to expand next round of negotiations to include European countries.

It’s a pretty chilly morning in Dublin, but the European Council president, António Costa, is keen to signal to his hosts that he’s ready to do business, showing off a cute Irish green scarf to Ireland’s Micheál Martin.

Today’s host, Ireland’s Micheál Martin, said discussions will focus on what Europe needs to consider any future Ukraine settlement a just and sustainable peace.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the substance of any peace agreement is as important as who represents europe. Security guarantees are a significant part of that, and also the reconstruction of Ukraine. Europe needs to be very clear in terms of what would constitute a sustainable peace for the continent, well into the future. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, he said the outstanding questions on europe’s priorities and representation need to be decided “in the next week or two. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on ai, he said the meeting will “explore the implications of ai, positive … plus the potential negatives, and the balance between regulation and innovation. ”.

Estonian prime minister Kristen Michal has warned that Ukraine faces “winter … like hell again,” with Russia “bombing everything” as he urged European leaders to double down on their backing for Kyiv.

Berdasarkan laporan, “putin has to change his goals because the war, aggression, and killing of women, children, and civilians would stop right now if he gave an order. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the european plan for a while [has been] quite simple: help ukraine push russia and so should it be. ”.

Michal warned that Putin’s attempt to discuss the broader European security architecture before agreeing to end the war is “a mental trap” by Russia’s Putin.

“Does anybody really think that Europe is a threat to Russia? This is not sane talk to be honest.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so, i would say that our red line is quite clear: we should have peace, on ukraine’s terms, and after that everything can be talked, but not before and not at the same time. ”.

The Estonian PM also said that if the EU needs to send its negotiators, the European Council president António Costa and EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas are “the persons to do it”.

Diungkapkan bahwa european commission president ursula von der leyen insisted it is “self-explanatory” that europe should be included in the peace talks on ukraine “to safeguard our interests, but also to support ukraine. ”.

“We will come forward as a commission with a proposal for the financing of the Ukrainian needs in 2027, and with the 22nd sanctions package before the next European Council,” she said.

von der Leyen also said today’s talks would focus on “the risks … but also the opportunities’ associated with the rise of AI.

EU leaders will continue talks on their diplomatic and financial support for Ukraine today, after Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged them to “pay attention” to Vladimir Putin’s demands on security.

European leaders meeting in Dublin on Thursday rejected calls that there was any need to recreate a European security architecture, while restating that Russia needed to stop attacking Ukraine.

European Council president António Costa summed it up:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “there is no need to reinvent the wheel. Europe had a functioning European security architecture until it was first, gradually undermined, and ultimately destroyed by Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, speaking to reporters the uk prime minister andy burnham said europe “in the wider sense” i. e not just the EU, would decide on its own arrangements.

Berdasarkan laporan, “in terms of the wider point, there was a very strong feeling that you know, russian demands to put the question of european security architecture or european security arrangements into this negotiation – that is not up for negotiation. It is for Europe to decide its own arrangements. Europe and Europe alone. And again, I am talking in the wider sense when I say that. ”.

Around 40 countries, most of the attendees of the European Political Community summit on Thursday, signed a declaration drafted by France declaring that European states “bear a primary responsibility and are assuming greater responsibility for the security of Europe”.

Berdasarkan laporan, eu leaders are continuing talks in dublin on friday, focusing on ai. But following interventions from Giorgia Meloni and Friedrich Merz, they will also discuss Europe’s role in international peace talks and the question of future financial support for Ukraine.

EU leaders are meeting in Dublin today for discussions on Ukraine and AI, among others, as they continue their search for a lead EU negotiator in any peace talks with Russia.

Their discussions are becoming increasingly urgent, after Ukraine and Russia have agreed to expand the next round of peace negotiations to include European countries, US envoy Jared Kushner said last night after meeting Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin.

“This will allow us to address the broader postwar European security arrangements alongside the territorial issues between Ukraine and Russia,” Kushner ​said ​later on X.

But, as he somewhat mockingly said on Wednesday,.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “if europe could identify one person to speak on their behalf, that would be a bigger achievement than getting the russians to include them in the negotiations. ”.

Let’s see what comes out of these discussions, with the leaders also expected to talk about AI.

Elsewhere, I am still keeping an eye on the Dutch government crisis as Rob Jetten works hard to avoid the collapse of his minority cabinet.

It’s Friday, 13 November 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.

#121. Four grizzly bears killed in Canada after fatal attack on mother and daughter

📅 11 Nov 2026

Four grizzly bears killed in Canada after fatal attack on mother and daughter

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cwg5r8zrm11mo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Between 10,000 and 13,000 grizzly bears are estimated to live in British Columbia (file image).

Four grizzly bears have been killed in connection with a fatal attack on a mother and daughter in the Canadian province of British Columbia.

Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her daughter Selah Reed, 20, died earlier this month after going on an afternoon walk in a trail area in Bella Coola.

The British Columbia Conservation Office Service (BCCOS) launched an investigation into their deaths and forensic testing has since confirmed a sow and her three cubs were responsible for the attack.

All four were destroyed "in accordance with provincial human-wildlife conflict response guidelines" to protect the public, BCCOS Inspector Jeff Tyre said in an update on Tuesday.

Mother and daughter die after suspected grizzly bear attack in Canada.

"Evidence from the investigation as well as animal DNA was analysed and conclusively linked to a sow and its three offspring," he added.

The attack "likely involved predatory behaviour", which Tyre said was "very rare".

He added that more than a dozen conservation officers took part in the investigation over the past week, amid "difficult terrain and weather".

Balcarras and Reed were "two peas in a pod" who "got along really, really well" and shared many hobbies, Balcarras' brother, Josh, told CBC.

"When Jenny hiked, Selah was right there beside her," he said.

Tyre said DNA testing also confirmed the four bears were not involved in a 2025 attack on a school group also in the Bella Coola area.

The incident in November of last year saw 11 people injured, two of them critically, while the bear responsible was never found.

"Today, we have learned from the BC Conservation Officer Service members that they have captured and euthanized the bears involved in the recent fatal attack," said Samuel Schooner, Elected Chief of the Nuxalk Nation, in a statement.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "we would like to thank the bc conservation officer service for their dedication and hard work to resolve this incident. This attack has been deeply re-triggering for our community members as we continue to recover from last year's attack. Our thoughts remain with the victims' families. ".

Kenya has reported no new confirmed cases since 20 October 2026.

Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient - the seventh to recover from the virus - marking a major milestone in efforts to contain the disease in the East African nation, which now begins a 42-day countdown to officially being declared Ebola-free.

It had confirmed its first ever case of Ebola early in October when a Kenyan businessman died within days of arriving in the capital, Nairobi.

Berdasarkan laporan, he had contracted the virus in the democratic republic of congo, where more than 5,000 people have died in an ongoing outbreak that began in may. His mother also subsequently died.

Kenya's health minister said 135 identified contacts of the infected patients had also completed their 21 days in isolation.

"Today with the discharge of the last patient we can confirm and tell the world that seven patients have recovered - and all contacts have completed their follow-up monitoring," Aden Duale said.

The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) described it as an important achievement in the regional response to the outbreak.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "this is an encouraging moment for kenya and for africa. We must sustain surveillance and vigilance until the outbreak is officially declared over," Africa CDC chief Jean Kaseya posted on X.

What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult?.

Kenya has reported no new confirmed cases since 20 October.

All the Kenyan cases were linked to the man who had travelled from DR Congo through Uganda, with health officials reporting no evidence of wider community transmission.

Those who have recovered following treatment included four healthcare workers.

Five patients were discharged on 3 November, followed by a sixth three days later, before the final patient was cleared on Wednesday.

Under World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines, 42 days must pass after the last patient tests negative and is discharged, or the last Ebola victim is safely buried, before an outbreak can be declared over.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the ebola virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days, meaning those exposed to the virus may not become ill for several weeks.

Duale said the government would maintain heightened surveillance at border crossings, airports, health facilities and communities throughout the countdown.

Emergency response teams will remain on alert across the country, while the health authorities will continue monitoring travellers arriving from affected countries.

Kenyans returning from Ebola-affected areas are required to complete electronic health declarations before travelling, undergo screening on arrival and spend 21 days in quarantine under the supervision of health teams.

The minister also urged countries that had imposed travel and visa restrictions to reconsider them - adding that Kenya had no intention of serving as a quarantine centre for another country.

In May, a Kenyan court suspended US plans to open an Ebola quarantine facility for American citizens.

Kenya has maintained that there is no need to restrict domestic travel, trade or public gatherings.

The outbreak has nevertheless disrupted international travel, with some Gulf countries introducing restrictions affecting travellers from Kenya and other African countries.

Saudi Arabia stopped issuing visas to Kenyan nationals in late October, prompting concerns among those seeking employment there.

Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) has announced that it is lifting its suspension on issuing new visas to Ugandan nationals, easing restrictions introduced in June.

But Ugandans will have to spend at least 21 days outside of Uganda before being allowed to travel to the UAE.

The UAE is also allowing certain students, diplomatic passport holders and Ugandan embassy employees to enter under approved health procedures.

Uganda, which shares a long and busy border with DR Congo, was among the countries first affected but declared its own Ebola outbreak over on 27 August.

The current outbreak in DR Congo has been caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way.

Questions remain over Ebola patient who travelled across three nations undetected.

#134. Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose

Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose

Tanggal: 04 Apr 2023 | Sumber: https://www.cnn.com/2023/04/04/asia/tsai-ing-wen-taiwan-mccarthy-meeting-analysis-intl-hnk/index.html

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

Diungkapkan bahwa “every time taiwan does anything that china doesn’t like, the chinese react with their own military coercion,” sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last august, with chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between beijing and taipei in the taiwan strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to wen-ti sung, a political scientist at the australian national university’s taiwan studies program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

Diungkapkan bahwa china thinks it's diplomatically isolating taiwan. It isn't.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

Diungkapkan bahwa that’s driven concerns, among some in washington, that beijing is preparing for an invasion, though china’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification. ”.

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, congress has been a pillar of increasing american support for taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

What you need to know about China-Taiwan tensions.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, china is also acutely aware that its actions toward taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of ukraine by russian president vladimir putin, a close diplomatic partner of xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

Berdasarkan laporan, “a reset in us-china ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility. ”.

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/12/win-win-deal-with-eu-could-be-done-andy-burmham-says

Prime minister says reset could be a deal ‘like the Brexit people thought they were voting for in 2016’.

Andy Burnham has said he believes a “win-win” deal could be done with the EU that could be “more like the Brexit that people thought they were voting for in 2016”.

The prime minister was meeting fellow leaders at the European Political Community summit in Dublin, ahead of a keenly anticipated EU-UK summit next week, where he hopes to bring Britain closer to Europe.

At the bilateral summit the EU and UK hope to sign deals on food and drink, emissions trading and a youth mobility scheme, but the question of tuition fees for European students remains a stumbling block.

Burnham said: “I believe there is a good deal to be done that could be a win-win for Britain and Europe.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the deal is not done, and there’ll be some long nights ahead in the next seven days. ”.

He said the reset would be about whether we can “take a step back to closer working relationships with Europe”.

Berdasarkan laporan, burnham added: “we ended up with a far harder brexit, i think, than people thought they were getting when they went to the polls. ”.

The EU has said the prized food and drink deal and emissions-trading agreement may not enter into force without a deal on tuition fees in which European students would pay domestic rates.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, burnham said it was a package deal, but would not be drawn on whether he accepted the link. If I can do anything to address the cost of living crisis, I should be doing it. “I’m going to be fighting hard for these benefits for Britain in the next seven days … they will make a real difference. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, he has previously said the food and drink deal, which will ease brexit red tape, will add 0. 4% to British GDP.

The prime minister also said David Cameron had been wrong to argue that Britain’s problems had “nothing to do with Brexit”, adding there would be “long nights ahead” to negotiate a reset with the EU before the summit.

Cameron, the prime minister who lost the 2016 Brexit referendum, told Bloomberg News that Burnham should not seek to bring Britain back into the EU, arguing that the UK’s problems had nothing to do with its exit from the EU.

Sebagaimana diketahui, asked about those remarks, burnham said: “i think he is wrong to say that the low growth that we’ve had over the last decade has, quote, ‘nothing to do with brexit’. I would say the evidence says otherwise.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “it feels like his intervention is more about unity in the conservative party than it is about fighting for the british interests. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, burnham has recently said he is open to rejoining the single market, customs union or to “go all the way” by rejoining the eu. He said a deeper relationship would be the outcome of future talks “and it will be in the outcome of that negotiation that then we will take a decision as a cabinet, on what, if anything, comes next”.

Earlier on Thursday, the EU foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, said she wanted to see Britain rejoin the EU, but warned that negotiations would not be easy after the “trauma” of the Brexit years.

Diungkapkan bahwa she said: “i would very much like to see britain back in europe, but, of course, we also have in the european union, a lot of, i would say, trauma from britain leaving, so the negotiations will not be that easy. ”.

Sign up for the Breaking News UK email to get newsletter alerts direct to your inbox.

Burnham is expected to make the EU reset the centrepiece of his white-tie speech at the lord mayor’s banquet on Monday night – though it will range widely across foreign policy challenges.

No 10 sources said the speech would be focused on the upcoming Brussels summit – and look ahead to the next stage in 2027 – rather than outline what a more permanent close relationship might look like.

Officials at the UK-EU summit will also discuss the agenda for the next round of the reset, expected to focus on a joint migration pact.

It could also target collaboration on law enforcement and borders, visas for touring artists, and mutual recognition of qualifications.

Berdasarkan laporan, ministry of justice officials are also trying to water down an eu ultimatum on halting the deportation of foreign national offenders. “This is the classic wheeze that the EU always pulls at the last minute of negotiations,” one Whitehall source said.

Diungkapkan bahwa the next week is expected to be fraught with last-minute negotiations. Key will be access to Made in Europe, which has the potential to lock British firms out of continental supply chains and public contracts if no deal is done.

Negotiations could be challenging despite the lure of the UK making a potential concession on tuition fees in exchange for inclusion in the Made in Europe legislation.

The EU has long said there cannot be a deal on Made in Europe at the summit, because it has yet to finalise its own position.

The joint communique for 2027 is expected to call for strengthening efforts between the UK and the most exposed member states to the small boats crisis in the Channel.

This will centre on both the EU’s Channel action plan, already in place since June this year, and a possible framework for a wider bespoke EU-UK migration plan.

The UK is believed to be pushing for access to the Eurodac database, which carries the fingerprints of asylum seekers, as well as to the Schengen Information System (SIS), which records details on fugitives, missing people and stolen goods.

The UK was the third biggest user of SIS before it lost access through Brexit.

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/nov/13/mohammad-javad-vafaei-sani-iran-boxer-death-row-magnitsky-award

Political prisoner Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, one of seven athletes at risk of execution in Iran, given prestigious Magnitsky humanitarian award.

A boxer and political prisoner on death row in Iran said he will “never surrender” as he accepted a prestigious human rights prize on behalf of “the generation that is paying the price of freedom with their lives”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mohammad javad vafaei sani, an iranian boxing champion, coach and political prisoner, has been sentenced to death three times and is one of seven athletes at risk of execution in iran. He was given the Magnitsky award for outstanding human rights activist at a ceremony in London on Thursday night.

Diungkapkan bahwa in a written message from vakilabad prison in north-eastern iran, he said: “i accept this award in the name of all those who, for the ‘crime’ of aspiring to a free iran, have been imprisoned, tortured, threatened, or sentenced to death; in the name of my comrades in the resistance units and the generation that is paying the price of freedom with their lives. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he added: “the regime demands repentance, televised confessions and surrender from us. But our answer is clear: ‘We will never surrender; we will never submit to humiliation. ’”.

Vafaei Sani, 31, was arrested in 2020 for taking part in nationwide democracy protests in 2019 and accused of supporting an opposition group, the People’s Mojahedin Organization of Iran (MEK).

Diungkapkan bahwa he was convicted of “corruption on earth” and sentenced to death for a third time in september 2024 after “a grossly unfair trial”, according to amnesty international. The supreme court upheld his death sentence on 4 October 2025. Since his arrest he has been tortured and held in solitary confinement for extended periods.

His continued imprisonment has drawn widespread international condemnation from prominent sportspeople, human rights organisations and legal experts who have called for his immediate release and the annulment of his death sentence.

Berdasarkan laporan, the magnitsky awards are named after the russian lawyer, sergei magnitsky, who died in russian police custody after exposing government corruption. They began in 2015 as a way to recognise journalists, politicians and activists in the field of human rights.

Diungkapkan bahwa sir william browder, head of the magnitsky justice foundation and the chair of the awards committee, said vafaei sani’s case was emblematic of the plight of many iranians who face execution for standing against the regime. Every time the world pays attention, it becomes harder to kill him quietly. “That is why this award matters. “Most important, Mohammad Javad is still alive,” he said. ”.

According to the Hengaw Organisation for Human Rights, at least 710 people have been executed in Iran since the beginning of 2026, including 79 political and religious prisoners.

Diungkapkan bahwa in an october report, the organisation documented at least 106 death sentences against january protest detainees, 35 of whom had already been executed. In Vakilabad prison, where Vafaei Sani is detained, five people have been executed linked to the protests and 15 others are facing death sentences.

Diungkapkan bahwa vafaei sani’s award comes at a time when there are growing fears for imprisoned iranian athletes, who are considered role models in the country. Zohreh Abdollahkhani, founder of Human Rights for Sport, said: “The situation is really dire … We have seven athletes at risk of execution now, including Vafaei Sani. ”.

#148. The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal

📅 12 Nov 2026

The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmze750zg0jeo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

BBC's Samira Hussain reports from Wall Street on what the fall of the tech superstar means.

Diungkapkan bahwa jensen huang, known for sporting a black leather jacket to shareholder events, appeared to have it all. He was courted by leaders in the US and China alike, worshipped by investors and seen as a loyal family man. But a rockstar approach to his personal life has ultimately led to his resignation.

The 63-year-old has been married since 1985, long before the foundation of Nvidia, the company that propelled him to tech stardom.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he is known as a workaholic and a demanding manager, with high standards for those who worked for him, which included his own children, promoted within the company. But he has seen his personal reputation go into freefall this week, undone by romantic entanglements that throw doubt on his focus and his judgement.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on thursday, he resigned following back-to-back revelations of two affairs. News of the first - a relationship with a businesswoman alleged to be a Chinese spy - ricocheted around the world, raising eyebrows among investors. It was followed on Wednesday by reports that the tech boss had also had an affair with an Nvidia colleague.

Diungkapkan bahwa his departure creates uncertainty in the global stock market, which was already knocked-off balance in recent weeks. Nvidia is a linchpin in the US's race for technology leadership with China.

Huang may not be a household name on the same level as Elon Musk or Mark Zuckerberg.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but his role in the tech industry, especially in relation to the explosion of artificial intelligence in the last three years, may prove more consequential. Nvidia dominates the market for the microchips that are used to power the new technology.

Berdasarkan laporan, the company, which is still valued at nearly $4n (â£3. 02tn) despite recent events, is at the centre of the AI race between the US and China, the world's tech and economic powerhouses.

Huang enjoyed access to the seats of political power on an unrivalled scale, being courted by both US President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping.

His remarkable rise to the top of his profession has led to him being dubbed the "Taylor Swift of tech" and seen him amass an estimated fortune of $145bn, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

Despite always donning his trademark all-black outfits and taking a playful approach to investor presentations, Huang has worked for years to present himself as a family man, someone who exemplified the American Dream.

Sebagaimana diketahui, born in taiwan in 1963, huang and his family moved to the west coast of the us when he was nine years old. He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a Master's degree in the same field from Stanford University.

Diungkapkan bahwa it was at college where he met his wife, lori mills. The pair were lab partners and married in 1985, eight years before Huang founded Nvidia.

They have two children, Madison and Spencer, who now both work in senior roles at Nvidia.

Diungkapkan bahwa the company became a key provider of the computer chips and circuits used for gaming before it expanded in a new direction. It now creates the key processing chips used to power the growing AI technology.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after tech giant rocked by second affair allegation.

Who could replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia's chief executive?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, huang has hailed ai as a "new industrial revolution" that is on par with the advent of electricity. Nvidia is the world's second most valuable company and its customers include the biggest firms on the planet, Google, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, SpaceX, Tesla, OpenAI and Anthropic, all spending big on its products.

So it is no surprise that at a recent AI summit at the White House, Huang was picked out from a group of 42 to flank the president, alongside Elon Musk, both men with whom Trump has famously close relationships.

Berdasarkan laporan, "jensen huang is a tech visionary of the likes of steve jobs," stephen witt, the author of thinking machine, a biography on jensen huang, told the bbc, referring to the late boss of apple. He added that Huang was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today.

He described him as a "demanding" boss, who "really pushes his people to the limit".

But while the former Nvidia CEO is "very brilliant" and a "world-class computer scientist", there's also "a level of arrogance" and "a level of self-deception as well", he said.

Huang had gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man, he added, something that was "very important to him".

Sebagaimana diketahui, "he praises his wife, he talks about her in very glowing ways," witt added. "The fallout of this would be bad for anyone's family. But for someone who has gone to such great lengths to cultivate an image of being a family guy and who keeps his children very close, it is very bad. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, first reports emerged on 29 october in the new york times that huang had conducted a relationship with alice huang, no relation. US officials allege the businesswoman associated with Singapore-based firm Megaspeed is a Chinese intelligence asset.

After the revelations of the first affair, Huang admitted to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting their family.

Diungkapkan bahwa trump, as well as other leaders in the ai tech industry, initially backed huang to continue in his role at nvidia. The president described him as "honourable".

But the reporting of a second affair, with Kimberly Powell, vice president of healthcare who has worked at Nvidia for 18 years, prompted a board meeting, followed by the announcement Huang was stepping down.

In the aftermath of that news Trump said Huang had done "a fantastic job" and proposed Tim Cook of Apple as a suitable replacement at the head of Nvidia.

#150. Two men found guilty of helping Iran try to ‘eliminate’ UK-based journalists

📅 12 Nov 2026

Two men found guilty of helping Iran try to ‘eliminate’ UK-based journalists

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/nov/12/two-men-found-guilty-over-iranian-attempts-to-eliminate-uk-based-journalists

Mostafa Sepahvand and Farhad Javadi Manesh carried out surveillance in an effort to inflict violence on targets.

Two men of Iranian origin who were hired through social media as part of a plan to “eliminate” journalists in the UK have been found guilty of assisting Tehran’s intelligence services.

Mostafa Sepahvand, 41, and Farhad Javadi Manesh, 46, carried out surveillance and reconnaissance between August 2024 and March last year in an attempt to inflict violence on “subjects” in the UK.

These subjects included two journalists for the London-based Persian broadcaster Iran International, Mojtaba Pourmohsen and Kambiz Hosseini, and a founder member of UK Lawyers for Israel, Jonathan Turner.

Berdasarkan laporan, the defendants visited addresses linked to their targets, took photos and videos and used platforms such as chatgpt to research them online. They appear to be part of a growing new tactic used by hostile states in which “proxies” are hired to work for foreign security forces, with often little idea who they are targeting or why.

Last month the Norwegian teenager Johannes Natland, 19, was jailed for life after he agreed to carry out a hit in Huddersfield for the Foxtrot Network, a Swedish organised crime group backed by the Iranian regime.

The Iranian men came to the UK illegally between 2016 and 2022 – Sepahvand in the back of a lorry and Manesh in a small boat.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sepahvand used the ai platform chatgpt to find the home address of pourmohsen, who worked for the london-based persian language broadcaster iran international. He hoped to be paid £150,000 to carry out a violent attack and help to “finish off” Pourmohsen.

Sepahvand chatted on WhatsApp to his handler, an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander called Amin, as he spied on Pourmohsen in December 2024, Woolwich crown court heard.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, amin wrote: “these are new pictures of the guy/bloke. ”.

Referring to a picture, Amin said: “And that dot is their office?”.

Berdasarkan laporan, sepahvand said: “love you brother, i’ll go there tomorrow. ”.

The pair also discussed surveillance of the Iranian satirist Kambiz Hosseini, who eventually had to leave home because of the threats made against him.

Sebagaimana diketahui, bill emlyn jones kc, prosecuting, said iran and its rulers did not and could not tolerate dissent. “One organisation critical to the regime, and therefore very much in its sights, is Iran International, a news organisation which has come under particular attack because of its explicit support for opposition groups and its editorial stance, which is anti-Islamic Republic of Iran.

Berdasarkan laporan, “eliminating hostile, critical or dissident actors overseas is a staple policy of the islamic republic. Together, the defendants were engaged in what is very obviously a form of spying,” Jones said.

Berdasarkan laporan, hosseini, 51, had to leave home and stop work as a standup comedian as a result of the threats he received. He was sent a message with a picture of his car saying the next time he started the engine it would blow up. Hosseini’s family in Iran also received threats, and his family had to leave the country.

The court heard Sepahvand had been convicted of theft in Iran and was drawn into the plan to “eliminate” dissidents in the hope of reducing his criminal record.

Sign up for the Breaking News UK email to get newsletter alerts direct to your inbox.

He told his Iranian handlers he was prepared to escalate from surveillance to violence, the court heard.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he hoped to receive a final payment of £150,000 for “finishing the job”, a reference to killing one of the journalists, the court was told. “If the person [the target] is inside, they pay the £150,000, and I’ll finish him off,” said Sepahvand in a voice note.

Berdasarkan laporan, sepahvand claimed his family was being threatened and that he never intended to go through with the hit. He also denied plotting to kill Turner.

Manesh claimed he took a picture of the Iran International site because it was “a beautiful building” and did not know they were working with the Iranian intelligence services.

Berdasarkan laporan, earlier this year, roman lavrynovych, 22, and stanislav carpiuc, 27, were jailed at the old bailey for seven and two years respectively for arson attacks on property connected to keir starmer. An anonymous Russian-speaking figure named El Money had recruited Lavrynovych and Carpiuc on Telegram.

Diungkapkan bahwa last year, six britons were jailed for their parts in a russian-ordered arson attack on a london warehouse providing aid to ukraine. The ringleader, Dylan Earl, was recruited by the Wagner group, a mercenary organisation that acts on behalf of the Russian state.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sepahvand was convicted by the jury of assisting a foreign intelligence service and preparatory conduct. Manesh was convicted of assisting a foreign intelligence service, but cleared of preparatory conduct.

Shapoor Noori, 57, of Ealing, was cleared by the jury of assisting a foreign intelligence service and preparatory conduct.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sepahvand, manesh and noori had claimed asylum in the uk and received temporary leave to remain. None of them had regular full-time employment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it is understood they met by chance and were then directed by sepahvand and his contacts in iran. There appeared to be no evidence of any wider plot.

Mrs Justice Cheema-Grubb remanded Sepahvand and Manesh before sentencing at the Old Bailey on 17 December.

The four astronauts NASA picked for the first crewed moon mission in 50 years

Astronauts who will helm the first crewed moon mission in five decades were revealed on Monday, queuing up the quartet to begin training for the historic Artemis II lunar flyby that is set to take off in November 2024.

The astronauts are NASA’s Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover and Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen of the Canadian Space Agency.

Berdasarkan laporan, wiseman is a 47-year-old decorated naval aviator and test pilot who was first selected to be a nasa astronaut in 2009. A native of Baltimore, Maryland, he’s completed one prior spaceflight, a 165-day trip to the International Space Station that had launched aboard a Russian Soyuz rocket in 2014. Most recently, Wiseman served as chief of the astronaut office before stepping down in November 2022, making him eligible for a flight assignment.

Wiseman will serve as commander of the Artemis II mission.

Diungkapkan bahwa hansen, 47, is a fighter pilot who was selected by the canadian space agency for astronaut training in 2009. From London, Ontario, Hansen is one of only four active Canadian astronauts, and he recently became the first Canadian to be put in charge of training for a new class of NASA astronauts.

He will be the first Canadian ever to travel to deep space.

Glover is a 46-year-old naval aviator who returned to Earth from his first spaceflight in 2021 after piloting the second crewed flight of SpaceX’s Crew Dragon spacecraft and spending nearly six months aboard the International Space Station.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “it’s so much more than the four names that have been announced,” glover said during the monday announcement at nasa johnson space center in houston. “We need to celebrate this moment in human history. … It is the next step in the journey that will get humanity to Mars. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, glover, born in pomona, california, served in several military squadrons in the united states and japan in the 2000s, and he completed test pilot training with the us air force. When he was selected for the NASA astronaut corps in 2013, he was working in the US Senate as a legislative fellow. All told, Glover logged 3,000 flight hours in more than 40 aircraft, over 400 carrier arrested landings and 24 combat missions.

Glover’s first mission to space was as part of the SpaceX Crew-1 team, which launched to the International Space Station in November 2020 for a six-month stay on the orbiting laboratory.

Diungkapkan bahwa koch, 44, is a veteran of six spacewalks — including the first all-female spacewalk in 2019. She holds the record for the longest single spaceflight by a woman, with a total of 328 days in space. Koch is also an an electrical engineer who helped develop scientific instruments for multiple NASA mission. Koch, a native of Grand Rapids, Michigan, also spent a year at the South Pole, an arduous stay that could well prepare her for the intensity of a moon mission.

Berdasarkan laporan, the artemis ii mission will build on artemis i, an uncrewed test mission that sent nasa’s orion capsule on a 1. 4 million-mile voyage to lap the moon that concluded in December. The space agency deemed that mission a success and is still working to review all the data collected.

Berdasarkan laporan, if all goes to plan, artemis ii will take off around november 2024. The crew members, strapped inside the Orion spacecraft, will launch atop a NASA-developed Space Launch System rocket from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

The journey is expected to last about 10 days and will send the crew out beyond the moon, potentially further than any human has traveled in history, though the exact distance is yet to be determined.

The “exact distance beyond the Moon will depend on the day of liftoff and the relative distance of the Moon from the Earth at the time of the mission,” NASA spokesperson Kathryn Hambleton said via email.

After circling the moon, the spacecraft will return to Earth for a splashdown landing in the Pacific Ocean.

Sebagaimana diketahui, artemis ii is expected to pave the way for the artemis iii mission later this decade, which nasa has vowed will put the first woman and person of color on the lunar surface. It will also mark the first time humans have touched down on the moon since the Apollo program ended in 1972.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the artemis iii mission is expected to take off later this decade. But much of the technology the mission will require, including spacesuits for walking on the moon and a lunar lander to ferry the astronauts to the moon’s surface, is still in development.

NASA is targeting a 2025 launch date for Artemis III, though the space agency’s inspector general has already said delays will likely push the mission to 2026 or later.

Berdasarkan laporan, the space agency has been seeking to return people to the moon for more than a decade. The Artemis program was designed to pave the way to establishing a permanent lunar outpost, allowing astronauts to live and work deeper into space long term as NASA and its partners map a path to sending the first humans to Mars.

Berdasarkan laporan, vanessa wyche, the director of nasa’s johnson space center, declined to provide details to cnn about the selection process. But she emphasized the diversity of the Artemis II crew, which includes men and women rather than only a staff of White male test pilots as has been the case for historic missions of the past.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i can tell you, they still all have the right stuff,” wyche said. “We have requirements different than we did (when we) just had test pilots” on inaugural missions.

Koch said in an interview with CNN’s Ed Lavandera that the group found out they were selected a few weeks ago.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we were all sent to a meeting that was on our calendars under a different pretext that didn’t sound as lofty as the one it was going to be,” koch said. “And accidentally two of us were very late to that meeting. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, she said the offer rendered her “speechless. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “it truly is an honor,” she added. “It’s an honor — not to get myself in the space — but because it’s amazing to be a part of this team that’s going back to the moon and on to Mars. ”.

An interview with the four astronauts will air on “CNN This Morning” on Tuesday, which starts at 6 am ET.

CNN’s Kristin Fisher contributed to this story.

#159. Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over?

📅 13 Nov 2026

Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over?

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cm3egjgvp794o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Pro-government forces marched into Tigray's capital less than two weeks after the war began.

Running a hair salon in Mekelle, capital of Ethiopia's troubled northern Tigray region, is not easy at the moment.

Diungkapkan bahwa "people can't prioritise beauty over daily basic needs. For many residents, thinking about self-care is a luxury, at a time when they can't feed their kids," Firut Me'ar, who runs a salon in the city, tells the BBC.

After a brief war, the city is under the control of the national army but life is far from normal, says Firut, a single mother of a 10-year-old daughter.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "things are better than during the war, but people still have no money, no morale. Business is almost non-existent," she says, her voice shaking with emotion.

Berdasarkan laporan, above all, she says people are worried about what the future holds. "There is uncertainty about what comes next. ".

Fighting broke out in late September between the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the party that had run Tigray for decades, and the national army - a resumption of the two-year civil war that officially ended in 2022.

Berdasarkan laporan, but within less than two weeks, federal forces marched triumphantly into mekelle. The TPLF made what it called a "strategic withdrawal" from the city and Tigray's other main towns so the army encountered little resistance. Hundreds of people are reported to have died in the conflict, including dozens killed by drone strikes and bombing raids by the air force.

Ethiopian government officials and supporters argue that the war is effectively over and that the only remaining task is to clear Tigray of TPLF elements.

Getachew Reda, a senior TPLF official who switched sides and is now an adviser to the prime minister, declared that the war in Tigray had ended and that stabilising the region should now be the immediate priority.

Cameroon Hudson, an analyst and consultant on African peace and security, says there are various reasons for the TPLF's rapid defeat.

Diungkapkan bahwa "the tplf has lost popular support at home. It is fragmented, it does not possess the advanced military technology necessary to match the ENDF [Ethiopian National Defence Forces]," he says. "It has lost many of its generals, strategic thinkers, finest diplomats and fighters, either through defections or arrests. The infighting within the TPLF leadership has caused significant damage. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa abraha hailezgi, a scholar at mekelle university, agrees. In recent years, it has become associated with coercion, abuses, forced recruitment and arbitrary actions. "The army lacks a clear political vision. As a result, many people have come to view the TPLF army as an adversary rather than a force acting on their behalf," he says.

Speaking by telephone from an undisclosed location, TPLF spokesperson Mikael Asgedom denies that the group has lost.

Diungkapkan bahwa instead, he describes it as a deliberate tactical and strategic retreat. "This is not a defeat," he tells the BBC.

Dozens of people were killed in drone strikes during the short conflict.

Berdasarkan laporan, he says the tplf "intentionally allowed the endf to advance deeper into the heartland of tigray", where it can be isolated and confronted on favourable terrain. "We chose not to fight on terms favourable to the enemy. ".

The TPLF is preparing for a major counteroffensive, he says, adding that TPLF fighters have launched attacks against Ethiopian forces in several locations following their withdrawal from the region's towns, arguing that these operations demonstrated the group's continued military capability.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it is hard to get verified information from tigray and the bbc is unable to report from there. But phone lines and the internet, which were cut when fighting broke out, have now been restored.

Residents in different parts of Tigray tell the BBC that fighting is continuing in central, northern and north-western parts of Tigray, with the use of heavy artillery and drone strikes.

Eyewitnesses around Sheraro, a town near the Eritrean border, report heavy fighting involving artillery and ground forces in recent days.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "we could hear heavy artillery fire from the sheraro direction. People are concerned because there is no sense of security," a businessman tells the BBC on condition of anonymity. He adds that military convoys from both sides had moved towards Sheraro, while a motorcycle operator in the southern town of Yechila says military checkpoints are still active.

Memories of the devastating 2020-2022 Tigray war remain raw for many residents.

The conflict saw widespread human rights abuses and allegations of ethnic cleansing in Western Tigray, while estimates suggest the war claimed hundreds of thousands of lives.

As soldiers from Eritrea, accused of some of the worst atrocities in the previous conflict, and Ethiopia have reappeared in Tigray's towns, many residents describe a profound sense of fear and anxiety, saying the sight of the troops has reopened still-fresh wounds.

Berdasarkan laporan, military sources aligned with the federal army say operations against the tplf are continuing, with recent fighting and troop movements reported in northern tigray, near the eritrean border, as well as across central tigray's rugged highlands. They claim the TPLF's capabilities are being steadily degraded.

Diungkapkan bahwa security analysts and observers agree that unrest is likely to continue for some time. "I see a situation in which there could be a prolonged war in Tigray," Yared Tibebu, a well-known Ethiopian commentator based in the US, tells the BBC.

Sebagaimana diketahui, yared argues that the tplf has a long history of waging protracted armed struggles and believes the movement is once again preparing for a lengthy conflict. He believes that once the group has reorganised its military and political structures, it may attempt to resume offensive operations.

However he believes this will not happen for some time because of internal divisions - a suggestion dismissed by TPLF spokesperson Mikael.

The army says it seized all these weapons from the TPLF during the fighting.

Diungkapkan bahwa hudson rejects the idea that tigray is heading towards a prolonged war but agrees that the region may not be truly peaceful for some time. "The TPLF may continue a low-level insurgency and guerrilla campaign, but that is not war. I do not think there will be a wider-scale conflict between the federal forces and the TPLF. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, he says the tplf no longer possesses the size, strength or military capability required to effectively confront federal forces, which he says have significantly expanded and modernised in recent years. "The TPLF has also lost much of its public support and cannot easily rebuild its ranks through recruitment," he says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, yared, on the other hand, points to the tplf's history of overcoming setbacks as evidence that the movement could recover to sustain a prolonged struggle. "The TPLF has overcome many major challenges in the past. It is wrong to conclude that it has no public support. It is a political movement with a history stretching back more than 50 years," he says.

Most Mekelle residents only have money for the basic necessities at the moment.

Berdasarkan laporan, what yared sees as a strength, hudson sees as a weakness, saying the tplf is still "trapped in the past", and continues to behave as a dominant party within tigray, even though the situation has changed. "It is a movement that has not evolved, modernised or expanded. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, while hudson argues that the tplf is not equipped to sustain a major military campaign, the tplf spokesman says the group obtains weapons and logistical supplies from the ethiopian military. "We seize weapons from our enemy, and the weaponry that has entered Tigray will, sooner or later, become ours. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, in early october, eyewitnesses told the bbc they had seen eritrean troops in tigray amid reports they were backing the tplf. However, they appear to have returned home and Hudson thinks the country would be wary of becoming further embroiled in the conflict.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "first, eritrea does not have unlimited resources. "Third, Eritrea would have to consider the risk of provoking a confrontation with Ethiopia if it openly backs the TPLF. Second, the TPLF is no more an effective military force, and Eritrean leaders may have concluded that supporting it at this stage would not yield significant military gains," he says. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, sources in the ethiopia army tell the bbc that senior members of the tplf's political leadership were briefly based in eritrea, however, they say the authorities ordered them to leave in early november, shortly after president isaias afwerki returned from russia. According to the sources, the move was driven by concerns that Ethiopia could use their presence as a reason to invade.

Hudson also argues that Eritrea's renewed diplomatic engagement with the US, whose relations with the TPLF have long been strained, could further discourage Asmara from providing meaningful support to the movement.

In September, seven Ethiopian rebel groups led by the TPLF announced the formation of a new coalition called the Alliance for Survival, aimed at removing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government.

Seven rebel groups from across Ethiopia have announced a new alliance.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, yared believes the alliance could give the tplf the strength to keep on fighting. "Its members can combine their strengths. The TDF [the TPLF's military wing] has leadership experience and organisational capacity, while Fano [an ethnic Amhara militia] is believed to have between 70,000 and 80,000 fighters.

"If conditions emerge that allow the forces to co-ordinate effectively, the TPLF's current difficulties may not last long," he says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, hudson, however, rejects that argument, insisting that the alliance is unlikely to alter the balance of power. "I don't think the TPLF can be saved by this alliance. The ethnic militias have not demonstrated the capacity, either individually or collectively, to pose a serious threat to federal forces. We should not underestimate the strength of the federal army," he says.

Abraha from Mekelle University argues that the conflict in Tigray will only truly be over if the federal government addresses the region's feeling that it has been marginalised, both economically and politically by the current government.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, many tigrayan elites and political observers remain wary of the federal government's intentions. They question whether the authorities in Addis Ababa are genuinely seeking to address Tigray's problems, or whether they are taking advantage of the region's weakness to boost their influence.

In the meantime, many ordinary people in Tigray say their priority is peace.

Diungkapkan bahwa "peace seems slow in coming. Most people are tired of politics. Whatever happens, we only want peace and a chance to rebuild our lives," says Firut from her beauty salon in Mekelle.
