#160. NAZA: how and where to watch the Guardian’s acclaimed Gaza documentary

📅 12 Nov 2026

NAZA: how and where to watch the Guardian’s acclaimed Gaza documentary

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/global/2026/nov/12/naza-how-to-watch-guardian-acclaimed-gaza-documentary

Film features testimony from 24 Israeli officials involved in surveillance and remote killing of Palestinian civilians.

Diungkapkan bahwa naza will be released in full on the guardian’s website for free in early december. Sign up here to be notified of the exact streaming date and to be sent a link to the film when it is live.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, naza is currently screening in cinemas all over the world. It has been shown by cinemas in 47 countries and seen by more than 1. 5 million people since its release last month, making it one of the most-watched documentary films with a theatrical release in 2026. The film has been offered to a number of distributors and cinemas in Israel but has not been screened there yet.

Sebagaimana diketahui, naza is a documentary featuring testimony from 24 israeli military intelligence officers and soldiers involved in the surveillance and remote killing of palestinian civilians during the war in gaza. The film’s title comes from an Israeli military acronym used euphemistically to refer to civilians expected to be killed in a military attack.

The interviewees detail the methods used by the Israeli military in Gaza, including AI-based systems built to identify large numbers of potential Hamas operatives, who were then bombed in their homes at night, in the knowledge that the attacks would also kill their families.

Sebagaimana diketahui, interviews were filmed at night on rooftops in tel aviv, on the condition of anonymity, because of the risks involved in speaking publicly. The appearance and voices of participants in the film have been digitally altered to disguise their identities.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the film was directed by the oscar-winning israeli directors yuval abraham and rachel szor and produced by the guardian. It builds on revelations first published by the Israeli-Palestinian magazine +972, the Hebrew-language news outlet Local Call and the Guardian newspaper between 2023 and 2025.

Berdasarkan laporan, abraham and szor were two of the four co-directors – with the palestinians basel adra and hamdan ballal – of no other land, which documents the destruction of masafer yatta, a village in the occupied west bank targeted by israeli forces. It won the Oscar for best documentary in 2025.

NAZA was co-produced by James Wilson and executive-produced by Jonathan Glazer, the team behind the Oscar-winning film The Zone of Interest.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, naza has received widespread critical acclaim and is selling out in cinemas across the world. In a five-star review, the Financial Times says that “journalism and film-making brilliantly entwine”. The New York Times says it is “tough to watch and impossible to ignore”, while New York Magazine describes it as “one of the most important films of our time”. British Vogue calls NAZA a “brilliant and harrowing film”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the film won the special jury prize at the venice film festival in september, where its premiere had a 25-minute ovation – a festival record. In November, it won the best political documentary from the Critics Choice Association.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the film, its directors and their confidential sources have faced fierce attacks from the israeli government and military. The prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has ordered the attorney general and the head of the Shin Bet security service to reveal the identities of sources interviewed and prosecute them for causing “harm to Israel’s diplomatic and security interests”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, netanyahu also threatened to strip abraham and szor of their citizenship, accusing them of treason. The Israeli military’s chief of staff, Eyal Zamir, said the military would “not allow soldiers to be made targets through lies and blood libels” and would use “every tool at our disposal” against the film.

Diungkapkan bahwa far-right groups have vowed to hound the film-makers on their return to israel and picketed szor’s family home. Some of the messages included explicit calls for violence, with one protester demanding the “death penalty for traitors”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the israeli military claimed there were “substantial errors” in the film and that it had relied on sources who had only a partial picture of the target approval process. It said that while AI was used to help identify targets in Gaza, final decisions on strikes, and the risk of civilian casualties, were signed off by officers.

In response, the team behind the film have revealed they spoke to more than 100 sources with knowledge of the military systems used in the war.

Diungkapkan bahwa the israeli government is promoting an online film project, called naza: the real story, which mimics the style of the genuine naza film and is hosted on a website called nazadocumentary. com. It is not the real NAZA documentary and has been misleading some viewers.

Berdasarkan laporan, initially, the rival film’s website falsely presented itself as a promotional page for naza itself, naming abraham and szor as the directors, and listing film festivals where the documentary was to be screened. The site now appears as a platform for the rival film, which has been promoted by Israeli embassies.

#162. Before Scott Colom, these two men were the last black US senators from Mississippi

📅 12 Nov 2026

Before Scott Colom, these two men were the last black US senators from Mississippi

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmde1y19g19do?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Why Democrat Scott Colomâs win in Mississippi Senate race is so significant.

After winning a close race in Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colom will become the state's first black US senator for more than 150 years, and the third in history.

It is a historic result in the deeply conservative southern state that last sent a Democrat to the US Senate in 1982, and had not seated a black senator since 1875.

Sebagaimana diketahui, colom follows hiram revels, who became the first black person ever to serve in the chamber when he was seated from 1870 to 1871, and blanche bruce, whose term ran from 1875 to 1881. Revels and Bruce were both members of the Republican Party.

Revels was chosen as Mississippi's first senator after the Civil War, serving for just over a year and campaigning strongly for racial equality.

Berdasarkan laporan, a few years later, bruce, who was born into slavery, became the first black person to serve a full term in the us senate. He remained in Washington after leaving the chamber and held a role in the Treasury.

Both terms came before the repressive Jim Crow laws began to enforce racial segregation across Mississippi and other southern US states.

Blanche Bruce (L) and Hiram Revels (R) are the two previous black senators to have been chosen by Mississippi.

A significant factor in Colom's victory was his success in mobilising young people and the state's large black population, who are expected to have turned out in high numbers.

In a victory speech, Colom referenced how Revels, who was a minister and served as a chaplain during the Civil War, gained support for his Senate campaign through his words.

"That's an example of the power of prayer, and through our history, there are so many people that lifted this state up through the power of prayer in very dark times," Colom said.

A portrait of Hiram Revels, taken in about 1870.

Berdasarkan laporan, prior to the result being called, the bbc spoke to students at jackson state university, a historically black college in mississippi. Many of them had voted for the first time and backed Colom.

"I really feel like a change is what we need," 18-year-old Jamyria Dunn said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "i've had some amazing days in my life," she continued, "but seeing mississippi, this state in particular, turn blue, would really bring a light to my heart that people just would not understand. ".

Democrat Scott Colom makes history as Mississippi's first black senator since 19th Century.

Hospital director says 28 wounded in attack on one of few remaining medical facilities in the strip.

An Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in southern Gaza killed six people, including a surgeon and a disabled man, and wounded 28 others, according to the hospital director.

The Israeli military carried out the attack on the hospital, in Khan Younis, early on Thursday saying in a statement it had struck a Hamas commander and other fighters there, without providing evidence.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the strike destroyed part of the surgery department, and caused extensive damage to several floors. Services were suspended in four departments: radiology, laboratories, surgical operations and inpatient surgical wards, according to Dr Ahmed al-Fara, hospital director.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the ceiling of one of the wards had caved in, while debris-covered beds lay next to medical instruments twisted from the force of the blast. In other rooms, piles of rubble and shattered concrete cluttered the floor and a hole was left in the floor, where the bomb penetrated the building.

Diungkapkan bahwa dr ayman abu ubaid, a surgical specialist at nasser medical complex, who was wounded in the attack, said: “the bombing caused thick smoke to fill the rooms and fires to break out, amid the groans of wounded and people’s screams. There were many casualties and blood everywhere … Most of us sustained injuries to our limbs, as well as shrapnel wounds in different parts of our bodies. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, ubaid said the strike came at about 12. 30am, without warning. “The patients in the department were all surgical patients waiting to undergo operations. The bombing happened at a time when they should have been asleep,” he said.

Among the dead was Rizk Abu Shaira, 52, a general surgeon who had featured in American Doctor, a documentary about doctors operating in Gaza.

Diungkapkan bahwa “dr rizk was in the american doctor documentary operating and serving his people. He lost his life doing that, he lost his life because he was doing that,” Dr Thaer Ahmad, who also featured in the documentary, posted on X.

Abu Shaira was killed alongside one of his patients, on whom he had operated.

Sebagaimana diketahui, nasser hospital is one of the last functioning healthcare facilities in gaza, after israeli bombing made most of the strip’s facilities unusable. Last year Israel also struck the hospital, killing five journalists in a double-tap strike on a location often used by reporters for filming. In all, the hospital has been attacked seven times since the war on Gaza began.

Diungkapkan bahwa the israeli military has accused hamas of using hospitals as command centres and to store weapons, an accusation the militant movement rejects. More than 1,700 healthcare workers have been killed in Gaza, while Doctors Without Borders (MSF) says Israel has detained hundreds of medics since 7 October 2023, with at least 95 still in custody.

About 90% of Gaza’s health infrastructure has been destroyed or damage by Israeli bombing, systematic destruction UN experts called “medicide”.

Attacking healthcare facilities and staff is illegal under international humanitarian law, though these facilities can lose their protected status if they are used for military purposes.

There is an increased need for healthcare during the winter months in Gaza, where rains have displaced people from their tents and increased communicable diseases in crowded encampments.

Already, Nasser hospital is lacking about 80% of its essential medicines and medical supplies, said al-Fara, its director.

Diungkapkan bahwa one of those killed in thursday’s strike was seif ghazi abu hatab, 29, who was admitted to nasser hospital on monday after a piece of debris fell on his back while he was helping clear rubble from a friend’s home. He was scheduled for surgery at 10am on Thursday, and was meant to receive further treatment abroad.

Berdasarkan laporan, “seif was a young man in the prime of his life. He wanted to live, rebuild his home and start a normal life, free from problems and suffering … Seif was killed after already losing two of his brothers and his father. His mother has now lost three of her sons,” said his cousin Tareq Abu Hatab, 37.

Berdasarkan laporan, israel launched the war in gaza after the 7 october 2023 hamas-led attack that killed about 1,200 people and took 251 hostage. At least 74,645 people have since been killed in Gaza and Israel has carried out a genocide in the strip, according to the UN independent international commission of inquiry on the occupied Palestinian territory.

Israel continues to carry out airstrikes in Gaza, killing more than 1,600 people since the October 2025 “ceasefire”, according to the Gaza ministry of health.

#169. 'It can kill us': Kenyans fear impact of El Niño with floods predicted

📅 11 Nov 2026

'It can kill us': Kenyans fear impact of El Niño with floods predicted

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c8wy9y37z30vo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Agnes Shikoli says she fears either drowning, or being crushed by her house.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "it flooded up to here in march," agnes shikoli says, pointing to a spot halfway up the 6ft [1. 8m] corrugated iron wall of her home in Kibera, one of the largest informal settlements in Kenya.

Her tiny house lies just a couple of metres from the Ngong river, which runs through this densely populated area in the capital, Nairobi.

The scars of floods in the long rainy season earlier this year can still be seen - including a broken TV in the corner which was immersed in water.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, tucked out of sight is a photo of her sister beatrice khalayi, 58, who died when intense rains caused widespread destruction in kibera. She was among more than 60 people across the country who lost their lives.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "someone called me to tell me that she had died of electrocution after her house flooded," shikoli recalls. "When I see a picture of her, I feel uneasy, that's why I keep it far from me, so I don't see it. ".

With Kenya's short rainy season now starting, Shikoli tells the BBC she is afraid - especially following warnings that the El NiÃ±o weather phenomenon could bring a new round of flooding.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "i feel like it can kill us. "They can fall on us, or the water can drown us. These houses aren't made of stone," says the 62-year-old. ".

Kibera - and Kenya more widely - are on the front line of preparations for the potential impact of El NiÃ±o.

Forecasters have warned that this year could see one of the strongest on record, bringing extreme weather to many parts of the world.

In southern Kenya, that means the threat of rains even more intense than usual.

Outside Shikoli's house, groups of men and women wearing high-visibility vests are shovelling and raking garbage out of the riverbed and disposing it far from the water.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this programme called climate worx, under the office of president william ruto, is meant to rehabilitate nairobi's rivers. Such exercises have intensified since August when warnings increased about the possible scale of this year's El NiÃ±o.

Rubbish clogging Nairobi's drains and sewers was seen as a major factor in the deadly floods earlier this year.

Similar work to unclog drainage systems is ongoing across Nairobi, a sprawling city built on hilly ground crossed by three major rivers.

But the workers have a huge task on their hands.

Blocked drains and inadequate sewage systems were widely blamed for the high number of deaths after the floods earlier in the year, as the excess rainfall had nowhere to escape.

The Nairobi County disaster management chief, Bramwell Simiyu tells the BBC that drainage systems have been "untouched for many years" and that removing the rubbish from them will save lives.

Floods disproportionately affect informal settlements in Nairobi, especially those near rivers, like Kibera and Mathare.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in most of these settlements, houses sit just a few metres from rivers. Some people, including Shikoli, live on the slopes of the river itself due to the constant expansion of the settlements. When flash floods occur, these houses are swept away, endangering the lives of their occupants.

Nairobi's drainage system has not been upgraded to deal with the rapid growth in the population and infrastructure over the decades.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the existing drainage system was developed 30 years ago to cater for a population of about 2. 5 million residents but we're dealing with about seven million in the daytime and 5. 5 million night-time," Simiyu says.

He adds that investment of up to $192m (Â£143m) is needed to upgrade the sewerage and drainage system entirely.

But there is little sign that either the cash-strapped national or city council will able to raise this kind of money.

Berdasarkan laporan, the nairobi river basin regeneration programme, a government programme aimed at restoring the city's rivers, found that settlements near rivers, and where there is weak enforcement of regulations, have increased flooding risks. It recommended a "buffer" to protect rivers and "humane relocation" of communities where necessary.

However, rising poverty has driven many people to live close to rivers.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "our worst case scenario looking at low-income settlements is that up to about 100,000 people are at risk," simiyu says. "Moderate projections is about 5,000 households or about 20,000 people may be at risk. ".

Anyone forced to leave their homes will be relocated to 167 designated holding grounds where a stockpile of relief food and supplies will be distributed, Simiyu says.

Nobody knows exactly when the rains will come - or how much rain there will be.

But Kenya's meteorological department warns that November is usually the peak rainfall month of the short rainy season, which normally lasts from October to December.

A regional forecast from the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (Igad) warned in September that there was "an 81% probability of a very strong El NiÃ±o during October-December 2026".

So far, the heavy rains predicted have not occurred but experts remain concerned.

In East Africa, this El NiÃ±o is being widely compared to a similar weather event in 1997-1998 which caused widespread flooding and destruction in Somalia and Kenya.

Berdasarkan laporan, weather forecaster jemima gacheru tells the bbc that is because temperature conditions in the indian ocean in the 1997 el niã±o and those recorded now are similar. This interaction, she says, has been seen to result in very strong rainfall.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "for this season we have a very strong el niã±o already in play in the pacific and then we have a positive indian ocean dipole," gacheru said. This is often called the "Indian NiÃ±o" because of its similarity to its Pacific equivalent and refers to the difference in sea-surface temperatures in opposite parts of the Indian Ocean.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "we expect to have some enhanced rainfall over several parts of the country. ".

The UN's migration body the International Organization for Migration (IOM) has warned that almost 900,000 people could be forced to leave their homes in Kenya this year, mostly because of the predicted floods.

Dozens of people died in floods in Kenya earlier this year.

Kenya is not the only African country worried about the potential impact of El NiÃ±o.

Berdasarkan laporan, in neighbouring somalia, the country's disaster management agency has warned that 1. 2 million people are at risk of displacement caused by extreme weather - including the risk of both floods and drought.

Diungkapkan bahwa the 1998 floods killed 2,000 people in somalia and forced a further 250,000 to flee their homes, according to the food and agriculture organization (fao). Up to 80% of crops were destroyed in some parts of the country.

The United Nation's famine warning system IPC has warned of the increased risk of food insecurity in Somalia due to supply chain issues exacerbated by the impact of El NiÃ±o.

Elsewhere on the continent forecasters fear El NiÃ±o could bring extreme heat and prolonged periods without rain.

It could cause a crisis for farmers across parts of West Africa, including the semi-arid Sahel region south of the Sahara, as well as in southern parts of the continent, where the risk of crop failure is high.

There are fears El NiÃ±o's impact will worsen existing issues.

Communities like Kibera are already grappling with poor housing and rampant poverty, while parts of Somalia are in the middle of a devastating drought.

National governments in many countries are doing what they can to prepare but the extent of El NiÃ±o's impact is impossible to predict.

Back in Kibera, Shikoli and her family are preparing for the worst.

Council officials have told them they should leave their home on the riverbank until the rainy season has passed but Shikoli makes just $2 a day selling groundnuts and fruit from a small stall next to the river.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "i want to move," she says. "But I don't have the means.

Diungkapkan bahwa "we just have to persevere and leave it to god. ".

Gitanjali, the collection of poems that won Tagore the Nobel prize that same year, was praised by the committee for its “profoundly sensitive, fresh and beautiful verse”. Tagore’s English translation was published in London that March and reprinted 10 times by the time the prize was announced in November.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, tagore’s life and works have, of course, been well documented, but a collection of material preserved in a private family archive is now being brought into public view for the first time at an exhibition by christie’s, opening in mumbai this month. The archive draws from Tagore’s visits to the family home of his protege, Maitreyi Devi, in the bucolic village of Mungpoo in Darjeeling between 1938 and 1940. He died in 1941.

The collection on display – artworks, manuscripts, letters, photographs and personal effects – offers an intimate glimpse into Tagore’s creative process and personal world in his final years.

I spoke to the exhibition curator, Nishad Avari, head of south Asian modern and contemporary art at Christie’s, about the stories behind the archive.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one instructive document avari points to is a manuscript from 1940. It appears to be a draft of Tagore’s memoir Chelebela or My Boyhood Days, in which he reflects on his life – from growing up in a large family in Calcutta (modern-day Kolkata) to the rapidly changing world ushered in by electricity and the motorcar.

For Avari, what stood out was how the ideas in the document echoed the educational philosophy Tagore put into practice in Santiniketan (or Abode of Peace), the experimental school he set up about 100 miles from the state capital.

“He speaks about how education is like being in prison and that it should be open and free … about the idea of wonder and even fear as inspiring creativity,” Avari told me.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “that’s a direct relationship to santiniketan and the open model of the school where people sat under trees with their gurus and learned in the open. Education didn’t feel like a restriction, prison or imposition,” he added.

Sebagaimana diketahui, avari points to another detail that makes this particular document valuable. Of the 10 complete manuscripts in the exhibition, it is the only one dictated to Devi, whose father was a close friend of Tagore’s. For Avari, this speaks to their close relationship and the trust he placed in her.

Diungkapkan bahwa “if you look at the collection as a whole, she has copies of almost every single one of his publications signed to her by him,” he says. The collection includes hundreds of letters, too: first between Tagore and her father, and later between Tagore and Devi herself.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there are doodles among corrections, avari explains, which show how his literary practice fed into his artistic practice. Alongside the manuscripts and correspondence are vintage photographs and personal effects, including a kurta and a lungi that Tagore left behind at the family home.

Sebagaimana diketahui, among the artworks in the collection is a portrait of devi, particularly notable because tagore’s figure studies were not generally attributed to specific individuals in the way that portraits by his nephews, abanindranath and gaganendranath, often were, avari said. There is also a landscape depicting the forests of Mungpoo, which Tagore embraced as a retreat.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on the international art market, tagore’s paintings command significant prices. 02m (Rs 12. This year, Sotheby’s sold one of his watercolours for £1. 97 crore), nearly four times its low estimate.

Institutions such as Visva-Bharati in Santiniketan and the National Gallery of Modern Art hold much of Tagore’s archival materials, making the discovery of a private archive particularly rare.

Berdasarkan laporan, he hopes that making these materials public will offer historians, scholars and admirers alike additional perspectives on tagore. “We hope to add to the understanding of the artist, their career, and in this case, of course, our understanding of the man beyond his art as well. ”.

Rabindranath Tagore and Mungpoo runs between 10 November and 18 December at Christie’s space in south Mumbai.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, politics | india has invited pakistan to attend the shanghai cooperation organisation’s civilisational dialogue forum in new delhi later this month, the indian express reported. It is the first invitation since the two neighbouring states engaged in a military conflict last year.

Berdasarkan laporan, law | twenty-one media organisations have challenged india’s privacy laws in court, arguing that the controversial provisions threaten press freedom, reuters reported. The petition warns that the law could expose journalists’ sources and force publishers to remove stories at the direction of authorities.

Niha Masih takes a look at the stories, ideas and news makers of modern India.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, academia | indian academic mahmood kooria, a lecturer at the university of edinburgh, is among this year’s recipients of the philip leverhulme prize in humanities. The £100,000 award recognises his work on the premodern Indian Ocean world.

A recommendation from someone with great taste.

Freddy Birdy, a copywriter whose delightful words have earned him a devoted Instagram following, recommends writer and historian Malvika Singh’s cookbook, Cooking for My Firefly.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “this book isn’t about recipes, though it does include them. It is a voyage through another time and place, tracing the social fabric of India of the 60s, 70s and 80s, trickling down to today. Told in Malvika’s beautiful prose, it takes us to a time when people entertained in homes, not in restaurants; when dishes were cooked in-house and there were no caterers or party planners. It is an archive of photographs, food, culture, gossip, movie stars, politicians, royalty, set against the spectacular backdrop of Malvika’s dining tables through the decades. I like to dip into it every now and then, much as one might do standing in a dark kitchen with the light of the refrigerator enticing you to midnight goodies. An era long before Instagram posts, WhatsApp invitations, celebrity chefs and food delivery apps, when the point of having a party was simply to have fun. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa indians lost rs 22,495 crore (£1. 77bn) to cyberfraud in 2025, Times of India reported citing data from the Home Ministry. While the figure is marginally down from the previous year, losses have risen sharply since 2023.

At a time when public anger has spilled into the streets, artist Aamir Aziz’s new track, Dopeher Blues (Afternoon Blues), captures the frustration and angst of a generation that has lived through many crises.

Berdasarkan laporan, aziz describes the song as an expression of a period of deep suffocation. Issues such as farmer suicides, unemployment and conflicts in Palestine and Kashmir, he told me, are things he has grown up with even as public attention shifts with the news cycle. It is also a warning, in part, against internet culture, where injustices risk becoming normalised.

Diungkapkan bahwa aziz, 35, works in acting, music and writing, and became an internet sensation with his defiant poem sab yaad rakha jayega (everything will be remembered) during the citizenship protests. At the heart of his new track is a note of defiance and hope: “We’ll find a way to sing,” he says, as he calls on everyone “to keep speaking up even in a climate of fear, misinformation and oppression. ”.

But from Friday, members of the public will finally be able to visit a pioneering command bunker that was ordered by Winston Churchill and proved a vital defence during the second world war.

Berdasarkan laporan, the fan bay plotting room, which is encased in concrete, housed the first land-based computer-aided targeting system. This acted as a “brain” for a gun battery that was used to defend Dover and attack German ships in the Channel, according to Jon Barker, who led the excavation project for the National Trust.

Barker was the first person to enter the bunker when it was rediscovered in 2017 after it had been secretly mothballed in 1957 and classified until 1981 owing to its military importance.

Berdasarkan laporan, “it was a tutankhamun moment for a conflict archaeologist,” he said. “We had done all this research on the people who had served there, and then suddenly you’re standing in their office. It was an exciting moment. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the plotting room and the artillery it controlled can be directly traced to churchill. Soon after his “fight them on the beaches” speech, he visited the Kent coast and was alarmed to observe enemy ships passing through the strait of Dover unchallenged.

At the same time, Dover was on the frontline of a Britain facing regular bombardment by enemy guns in occupied France.

Berdasarkan laporan, in a july 1940 memo churchill wrote: “we have to fight for command of the straits by artillery, to destroy the enemy batteries and fortify our own. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he ordered the most advanced technology to be used and demanded weekly updates on progress on dover’s new defences. The guns were ready within 100 days and the plotting room bunker was completed 64 days later.

“The guns were known around here as Churchill’s pets,” Barker said.

Berdasarkan laporan, physical traces of the urgency of the construction were still visible at the site, said barker. He pointed to the rough openings through the walls and floors for the cabling. Contemporary accounts describe how the equipment was installed before drawings governing its layout were available.

Diungkapkan bahwa the plotting room housed a 1. 8-metre-long electromechanical computer known as a fire direction table. It was used to calculate the position of moving ships when shells hit and to send firing instructions to gun crews.

Diungkapkan bahwa barker said the discovery of the plotting room reminded him of the rescue of bletchley park, the codebreaking site in buckinghamshire, in the 1990s. “We didn’t know about it then, but now it’s all part of our national consciousness,” he said. “The plotting room is a new hidden history. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, he added: “we tend to think of plotting tables as glamorous wrens [members of the women’s royal naval service] pushing around markers on a map as they do in war films. But it’s not a map – it’s a really cutting edge electromechanical computer, and it is completely unique. ”.

The computer was deliberately destroyed in 1957 to stop it falling into enemy hands.

Sign up for the Breaking News UK email to get newsletter alerts direct to your inbox.

Sebagaimana diketahui, up to 10 people at a time worked in the plotting room. Barker is keen to make contact with anyone who had family members who served there, to help him understand how the machine worked.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “what we know about it is based on a manual and ghost markings on the floor. I would really love to hear if anybody knows if their family members served at Fan Bay because the records are scant. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the identities of only a handful of people who operated the computer are known. They include Wallas Eaton, an actor who later appeared as Senator Ludicrus Sextus in the TV comedy series Up Pompeii, alongside Frankie Howerd.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a man named wp bryant, a lance bombardier, was also recorded as a plotter at fan bay. “He was a tailor so he probably had a head for numbers,” said Barker.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the plotting room, which from friday can be visited via national trust guided tours through a hatch in a field, has been preserved as barker and his team found it. There is also chalked graffiti on one of the service tunnels saying “heroes fan hole Dodds and Petitt”. Remnants include old newspapers found on the floor, old shoes and official notices. Barker said Dodds and Petitt may have been involved in installing cables to the bunker.

“They were probably self-appointed heroes responsible for marshalling horrible thick cable through particularly uncomfortable tunnels,” he said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “there’s something very special about standing in a place that has changed so little since the people who worked here left. Rather than recreate the past, we’ve carefully conserved the plotting room so visitors can experience it much as we found it, with all the marks of its history still visible. It’s a rare opportunity to discover a completely different side of the white cliffs. ”.

#194. Hundreds of millions at risk from Chinese shopping app malware

📅 02 Apr 2023

Hundreds of millions at risk from Chinese shopping app malware

Tanggal: 02 Apr 2023 | Sumber: https://cnn.it/40OSomK

It is one of China’s most popular shopping apps, selling clothing, groceries and just about everything else under the sun to more than 750 million users a month.

But according to cybersecurity researchers, it can also bypass users’ cell phone security to monitor activities on other apps, check notifications, read private messages and change settings.

And once installed, it’s tough to remove.

While many apps collect vast troves of user data, sometimes without explicit consent, experts say e-commerce giant Pinduoduo has taken violations of privacy and data security to the next level.

In a detailed investigation, CNN spoke to half a dozen cybersecurity teams from Asia, Europe and the United States — as well as multiple former and current Pinduoduo employees — after receiving a tipoff.

Berdasarkan laporan, multiple experts identified the presence of malware on the pinduoduo app that exploited vulnerabilities in android operating systems. Company insiders said the exploits were utilized to spy on users and competitors, allegedly to boost sales.

“We haven’t seen a mainstream app like this trying to escalate their privileges to gain access to things that they’re not supposed to gain access to,” said Mikko Hyppönen, chief research officer at WithSecure, a Finnish cybersecurity firm.

Diungkapkan bahwa “this is highly unusual, and it is pretty damning for pinduoduo. ”.

This is highly unusual, and it is pretty damning for Pinduoduo.

Malware, short for malicious software, refers to any software developed to steal data or interfere with computer systems and mobile devices.

Evidence of sophisticated malware in the Pinduoduo app comes amid intense scrutiny of Chinese-developed apps like TikTok over concerns about data security.

Some American lawmakers are pushing for a national ban on the popular short-video app, whose CEO Shou Chew was grilled by Congress for five hours last week about its relations with the Chinese government.

Berdasarkan laporan, the revelations are also likely to draw more attention to pinduoduo’s international sister app, temu, which is topping us download charts and fast expanding in other western markets. Both are owned by Nasdaq-listed PDD, a multinational company with roots in China.

While Temu has not been implicated, Pinduoduo’s alleged actions risk casting a shadow over its sister app’s global expansion.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there is no evidence that pinduoduo has handed data to the chinese government. But as Beijing enjoys significant leverage over businesses under its jurisdiction, there are concerns from US lawmakers that any company operating in China could be forced to cooperate with a broad range of security activities.

The findings follow Google’s suspension of Pinduoduo from its Play Store in March, citing malware identified in versions of the app.

An ensuing report from Bloomberg said a Russian cybersecurity firm had also identified potential malware in the app.

Sebagaimana diketahui, pinduoduo has previously rejected “the speculation and accusation that pinduoduo app is malicious. ”.

CNN has contacted PDD multiple times over email and phone for comment, but has not received a response.

Pinduoduo, which boasts a user base that accounts for three quarters of China’s online population and a market value three times that of eBay (EBAY), wasn’t always an online shopping behemoth.

Berdasarkan laporan, founded in 2015 in shanghai by colin huang, a former google employee, the startup was fighting to establish itself in a market long dominated by e-commerce stalwarts alibaba (baba) and jd. com (JD).

It succeeded by offering steep discounts on friends-and-family group buying orders and focusing on lower-income rural areas.

Sebagaimana diketahui, pinduoduo posted triple digit growth in monthly users until the end of 2018, the year it listed in new york. By the middle of 2020, though, the increase in monthly users had slowed to around 50% and would continue to decline, according to its earnings reports.

It was in 2020, according to a current Pinduoduo employee, that the company set up a team of about 100 engineers and product managers to dig for vulnerabilities in Android phones, develop ways to exploit them — and turn that into profit.

According to the source, who requested anonymity for fear of reprisals, the company only targeted users in rural areas and smaller towns initially, while avoiding users in megacities such as Beijing and Shanghai.

“The goal was to reduce the risk of being exposed,” they said.

By collecting expansive data on user activities, the company was able to create a comprehensive portrait of users’ habits, interests and preferences, according to the source.

This allowed it to improve its machine learning model to offer more personalized push notifications and ads, attracting users to open the app and place orders, they said.

The team was disbanded in early March, the source added, after questions about their activities came to light.

PDD didn’t reply to CNN’s repeated requests for comment on the team.

Sebagaimana diketahui, approached by cnn, researchers from tel aviv-based cyber firm check point research, delaware-based app security startup oversecured and hyppönen’s withsecure conducted independent analysis of the 6. 49. 0 version of the app, released on Chinese app stores in late February.

Diungkapkan bahwa google play is not available in china, and android users in the country download their apps from local stores. In March, when Google suspended Pinduoduo, it said it had found malware in off-Play versions of the app.

The researchers found code designed to achieve “privilege escalation”: a type of cyberattack that exploits a vulnerable operating system to gain a higher level of access to data than it’s supposed to have, according to experts.

“Our team has reverse engineered that code and we can confirm that it tries to escalate rights, tries to gain access to things normal apps wouldn’t be able to do on Android phones,” said Hyppönen.

Diungkapkan bahwa the app was able to continue running in the background and prevent itself from being uninstalled, which allowed it to boost its monthly active user rates, hyppönen said. It also had the ability to spy on competitors by tracking activity on other shopping apps and getting information from them, he added.

Check Point Research additionally identified ways in which the app was able to evade scrutiny.

The app deployed a method that allowed it to push updates without an app store review process meant to detect malicious applications, the researchers said.

They also identified in some plug-ins the intent to obscure potentially malicious components by hiding them under legitimate file names, such as Google’s.

“Such a technique is widely used by malware developers that inject malicious code into applications that have legitimate functionality,” they said.

Berdasarkan laporan, in china, about three quarters of smartphone users are on the android system. Apple (AAPL)’s iPhone has 25% market share, according to Daniel Ives of Wedbush Securities.

Sergey Toshin, the founder of Oversecured, said Pinduoduo’s malware specifically targeted different Android-based operating systems, including those used by Samsung, Huawei, Xiaomi and Oppo.

CNN has reached out to these companies for comment.

Toshin described Pinduoduo as “the most dangerous malware” ever found among mainstream apps.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i’ve never seen anything like this before. It’s like, super expansive,” he said.

Most phone manufacturers globally customize the core Android software, the Android Open Source Project (AOSP), to add unique features and applications to their own devices.

Sebagaimana diketahui, toshin found pinduoduo to have exploited about 50 android system vulnerabilities. Most of the exploits were tailor made for customized parts known as the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) code, which tends to be audited less often than AOSP and is therefore more prone to vulnerabilities, he said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, pinduoduo also exploited a number of aosp vulnerabilities, including one which was flagged by toshin to google in february 2022. Google fixed the bug this March, he said.

Berdasarkan laporan, i’ve never seen anything like this before. It’s like, super expansive.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, according to toshin, the exploits allowed pinduoduo access to users’ locations, contacts, calendars, notifications and photo albums without their consent. They were also able to change system settings and access users’ social network accounts and chats, he said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, of the six teams cnn spoke to for this story, three did not conduct full examinations. But their primary reviews showed that Pinduoduo asked for a large number of permissions beyond the normal functions of a shopping app.

They included “potentially invasive permissions” such as “set wallpaper” and “download without notification,” said René Mayrhofer, head of the Institute of Networks and Security at the Johannes Kepler University Linz in Austria.

Diungkapkan bahwa suspicions about malware in pinduoduo’s app were first raised in late february in a report by a chinese cybersecurity firm called dark navy. Even though the analysis didn’t directly name the shopping giant, the report spread quickly among other researchers, who did name the company. Some of the analysts followed up with their own reports confirming the original findings.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, soon after, on march 5, pinduoduo issued a new update of its app, version 6. 50. 0, which removed the exploits, according to two experts who CNN spoke to.

Two days after the update, Pinduoduo disbanded the team of engineers and product managers who had developed the exploits, according to the Pinduoduo source.

Berdasarkan laporan, the next day, team members found themselves locked out of pinduoduo’s bespoke workplace communication app, knock, and lost access to files on the company’s internal network. Engineers also found their access to big data, data sheets and the log system revoked, the source said.

Diungkapkan bahwa most of the team were transferred to work at temu. They were assigned to different departments at the subsidiary, with some working on marketing or developing push notifications, according to the source.

A core group of about 20 cybersecurity engineers who specialize in finding and exploiting vulnerabilities remain at Pinduoduo, they said.

Toshin of Oversecured, who looked into the update, said although the exploits were removed, the underlying code was still there and could be reactivated to carry out attacks.

Pinduoduo has been able to grow its user base against a backdrop of the Chinese government’s regulatory clampdown on Big Tech that began in late 2020.

That year, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology launched a sweeping crackdown on apps that illegally collect and use personal data.

In 2021, Beijing passed its first comprehensive data privacy legislation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the personal information protection law stipulates that no party should illegally collect, process or transmit personal information. They’re also banned from exploiting internet-related security vulnerabilities or engaging in actions that endanger cybersecurity.

Pinduoduo’s apparent malware would be a violation of those laws, tech policy experts say, and should have been detected by the regulator.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “this would be embarrassing for the ministry of industry and information technology, because this is their job,” said kendra schaefer, a tech policy expert at trivium china, a consultancy. “They’re supposed to check Pinduoduo, and the fact that they didn’t find (anything) is embarrassing for the regulator. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the ministry has regularly published lists to name and shame apps found to have undermined user privacy or other rights. It also publishes a separate list of apps that are removed from app stores for failing to comply with regulations.

Pinduoduo did not appear on any of the lists.

They’re supposed to check Pinduoduo, and the fact that they didn’t find (anything) is embarrassing for the regulator.

CNN has reached out to the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and the Cyberspace Administration of China for comment.

On Chinese social media, some cybersecurity experts questioned why regulators haven’t taken any action.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “probably none of our regulators can understand coding and programming, nor do they understand technology. You can’t even understand the malicious code when it’s shoved right in front of your face,” a cybersecurity expert with 1. 8 million followers wrote last week in a viral post on Weibo, a Twitter-like platform.

CNN’s Kristie Lu Stout and Sean Lyngaas contributed reporting.

#199. The $500 billion beauty industry's 'green' ambitions are a patchwork at best. And they're falling short

📅 03 Apr 2023

The $500 billion beauty industry's 'green' ambitions are a patchwork at best. And they're falling short

Tanggal: 03 Apr 2023 | Sumber: https://www.cnn.com/style/article/beauty-skincare-climate/index.html

The escalating climate crisis is shifting many people’s purchasing patterns and this extends to the $500 billion dollar global beauty industry which is grappling with a range of sustainability challenges across product manufacturing, packaging and disposal.

Berdasarkan laporan, 'delay means death': we're running out of ways to adapt to the climate crisis, new report shows. Here are the key takeaways.

Strategy and consulting firm Simon Kucher’s Global Sustainability Study 2021 found 60% of consumers around the world rated sustainability as an important purchase criterion, and 35% were willing to pay more for sustainable products or services.

This shift in consumer preferences has propelled many beauty brands to set environmental goals: to move away from single-use and virgin plastics, provide recyclable, reusable and refillable packaging and offer more transparency around products’ ingredients so customers can ascertain how “green” their purchase is.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, consumers still struggle to understand the sustainability credentials of many products, according to the british beauty council. This is because the industry’s clean-up efforts have been inconsistent, and fall short of making a recognizable impact in the absence of collective goal-setting, global strategy and standardized regulations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there is no international standard for the beauty industry on how much product ingredient information to share with customers — or how to do so. Brands can set their own rules and goals, giving rise to confusion and “greenwashing,” where sustainability claims are often touted but not substantiated.

Companies often use marketing language like “clean beauty” to make it seem like their products are natural, for example, when they may not actually be organic, sustainable or ethically made.

After rebranding in the West, many beauty companies are still offering to 'whiten' skin elsewhere.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the term ‘clean beauty’ has become quite dangerous. “Customers need better marketing information and certification information. It’s used to sell more products,” according to British Beauty Council CEO Millie Kendall, who added that such buzzwords are losing traction in the UK as British customers wise up to their shortcomings. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in a 2021 report calling on the industry to have “the courage to change” their business practices, the british beauty council wrote that, all too often, even natural ingredients involved in manufacturing products give way to “over-consumption, non-regenerative farming practices, pollution, waste and neglect. ”.

“The only way out of this is transparency,” Kendall told CNN.

Diungkapkan bahwa jen lee, chief impact officer at us-based brand beautycounter, said she continues to see confusion over ingredients among consumers. (In 2013, the company launched and published “The Never List,” which currently cites more than 2,800 chemicals — including heavy metals, parabens and formaldehyde — it claims to never use in its products. ).

Diungkapkan bahwa “natural vs. synthetic ingredients has been a conversation. “Natural ingredients formulated in the industry can have toxic load. Heavy metals can occur in natural components of the earth. People think natural is safer, but it’s not always the case,” Lee explained. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, mother loses peripheral vision from apparent exposure to mercury in beauty creams. Toxic levels in her home put family at risk, say experts.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we used to be more natural and organic,” added sasha plavsic, founder of makeup brand ilia beauty. “What was challenging is (that) raw materials were difficult to source or would come in inconsistently or products wouldn’t perform. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, most makeup is created and molded at high temperatures, plavsic explained. “Not every synthetic is bad,” Plavsic said. Purely organic materials often fall apart in this heat, leading to inconsistent results and subpar product performance. “Sometimes, it helps create the best in class formula. ”.

The industry’s plastic packaging is a particular sustainability challenge — 95% is thrown away and the vast majority is not recycled, according to the British Beauty Council.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the cosmetics business is the fourth biggest plastic packaging user globally — after food and beverage, industrial packaging and pharmaceuticals — and plastic is about 67% of the industry’s packaging volume, according to vantage market research. Beauty giant L’Oreal used 144,430 metric tons of plastic in its packaging material in 2021, for example, according to the Ellen Macarthur Foundation (EMF). Estee Lauder Companies reported its brands produced 71,600 metric tons of plastic in product packaging that same year.

Berdasarkan laporan, and only 9% of the global plastic waste is recycled, according to a report from the organisation for economic co-operation and development. The United States only recycles 4% of its plastic waste.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, single-use plastic is wreaking havoc on the planet. Here's what you can do to minimize your impact.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, many brands are trying to phase out harmful plastics from their operations and adopt post-consumer recycled (pcr) plastic. (L’Oreal has set a target of 50% PCR plastic usage by 2025, while Estee Lauder is targeting 25% “or more” PCR plastic — but both are far from achieving their targets. ).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “between 60-70 major global brands have made unprecedented progress” in pcr plastic usage across industries, emf’s plastic initiative lead sander defruyt told cnn. But DeFruyt stressed that PCR plastic must be adopted in conjunction with brands removing single and virgin plastics from their usage cycles to truly make a difference.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, pcr plastic is not easy to find — low recycling rates around the world mean there is limited supply. Meanwhile, demand for it is growing demand across industries, DeFruyt said. This competition hikes up its price, which is already higher than virgin plastic.

Hair care brand FEKKAI claims that it used up to 95% PCR content in its packaging, but pricing and supply issues posed a challenge, forcing it to currently aim for containers and packaging that feature at least 50% PCR in its packaging.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “pcr plastic is more expensive than stock plastic. The cost is hard and then sourcing it is too,” founder Frédéric Fekkai told CNN. “PCR is close to our heart, but there is a massive demand, so finding recycled plastic is difficult. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, beauty retailers plays a pivotal — and under-utilized — role, with control over stocking decisions and supply chains. But many vary when it comes to the standards they set for brands they sell.

Berdasarkan laporan, “smaller businesses do more, full stop,” said jessi baker, founder of the technology platform provenance, which helps brands display their sustainability credentials for customers. They don’t need to restructure their entire supply chain. Some of them are born-good brands — climate friendliness was part of their setup. “They move more nimbly. Their culture already has it compared to the larger brands who need to work hard to change. ”.

A history of beauty trends -- and the standards that shaped them.

Berdasarkan laporan, sephora launched its “clean + planet positive” initiative in 2021, which labeled products that met its set criteria. (This is separate from the French retailer’s “Clean at Sephora” program, which is currently facing a consumer lawsuit alleging it carries a significant percentage of products understood by customers to be harmful. ) Target launched a similar program in 2022, featuring a “Target Zero” icon for both online and in-store offerings that either have reusable, recyclable, compostable or reduced plastic packaging, or feature waterless or concentrated products.

Still, many steps taken by brands and retailers do not even begin to touch on the waste and pollution generated throughout supply chains, manufacturing and shipping, all huge problems for the industry to grapple with.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the gaps in standardization in the beauty ecosystem can, to some extent, be filled by certifications such as the us-born b corporation, or b corp. This accreditation, one of the most well-known in the beauty space, is issued by the non-profit B Lab, which scores a company on a variety of criteria around ethics and sustainability. However beneficial it may be among eco-conscious consumers, though, it is currently completely voluntary for brands to apply for.

Governments and multinationals enforcing regulations and setting a base line for brands to operate from when making sustainability claims would go a long way to making change, many experts and business leaders believe.

Susanne Kaufmann, founder of her namesake beauty brand, says her efforts in Austria would reap better results if more countries around the world had stricter, more uniform garbage disposal laws.

A trash heap 62 meters high shows the scale of India's climate challenge.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i package our product in a recyclable material,” kaufmann said. (Her products’ packaging, which is refillable and reusable, is made from 75% recycled plastic — and is 100% recyclable. ) If I send this to the US, the garbage is not separated… and it’s not recyclable,” she explained, referring to inconsistencies in recycling laws across the United States.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and when it comes to ingredients, the european chemicals agency lists 2,495 substances banned from use in cosmetic products marketed for sale or use in the bloc. But the US Food and Drug administration only lists 11, making it more challenging for American consumers to find safer, greener options. The Environmental Working Group, a non-profit watchdog, studied lab tests of 51 sunscreen products in 2021 and found that only 35% of products met the EU standard, compared with 94% that passed the US standard.

However, while government can set minimum requirements, Mia Davis, vice president of sustainability and impact at beauty retailer Credo Beauty, says the needle will move in the private sector.

Sustainable ships: The world's most eco-conscious cruises.

Diungkapkan bahwa “regulation can raise the floor a bit. A person who doesn’t know about any (sustainability issues) should still be able to walk into a bodega and get clean products… But that’s never going to be what the market can do,” she said. “Market leadership is key. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the absence of bold regulations or global standards on sustainability practices, this “leadership” — undertaken both by brands and customers in the beauty marketplace — is likely to be the most immediately impactful vector for addressing the industry’s climate shortcomings. It will take continued collective advocacy and initiative to see meaningful climate-conscious change.

A ruling by a British-based court has invalidated laws criminalizing homosexuality in Trinidad and Tobago, setting a precedent for those challenging similar laws in other nations in the Caribbean and possibly beyond.

The ruling was handed down on Tuesday by the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London, which serves as the highest court of appeal for dozens of crown dependencies, overseas territories and former British colonies.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, five british judges unanimously upheld a 2018 decision by a lower court in trinidad that had found two sections of the caribbean country’s 1986 law targeting private, consensual same-sex relations to be unconstitutional. An appeals court in Trinidad had reversed the lower-court decision in 2025.

Trinidad’s attorney general had argued that the law preserved traditional family values in the country, and had leaned on a legal mechanism called “savings provisions,” which kept many laws from the British colonial era.

The battle pits a progressive Democrat, Van Hollen, against a centrist, Schumer, in the wake of Senate wins for progressive Democrats in Michigan and Maine who were not initially supported by Schumer.
