Congressman Jamie Raskin, a Maryland Democrat and the incoming chair of the House judiciary committee, told reporters on Thursday that one of his first priorities will be investigating the Trump administration firings of career justice department employees.

“That’s something that is central,” Raskin said of the firings that have taken place over the last two years.

Berdasarkan laporan, the maryland congressman said he expects, with majorities in both chambers of congress, democrats will have more authority to hold the administration accountable through the “power of the purse. ”.

Raskin is in Denver with other Democrats to discuss the next steps after winning majorities in the House and Senate.

In a friendly, softball interview with the sports pundit Stephen A Smith on Thursday at the White House, Donald Trump defended the Iran war with a big lie, and deflected blame for his party’s midterm losses with misinformation.

On Iran, Trump falsely claimed, as he has repeatedly, that the war he started in February was essential to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.

In fact, US intelligence agencies reported to Congress in 2025 that it was their assessment that “Iran is not building a nuclear weapon” and that the country’s supreme leader at the time, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei “has not reauthorized the nuclear weapons program he suspended in 2003”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, three months after that assessment was written, trump ordered the us bombing of suspected uranium enrichment sites in iran, which could be used for peaceful energy purposes or weapons making, and declared in june 2025 that “iran’s key nuclear enrichment facilities have been completely and totally obliterated. ”.

Speaking to Smith on Thursday, however, Trump claimed that the war he started with Iran just eight months later, in February, was necessary because of “the nuclear weapon that they were two weeks away from having”.

There is no public evidence that Iran had restarted the nuclear weapons program it suspended 23 years ago, but the rhetorical device of claiming that the regime was close to having a weapon has been deployed, for three decades, by Israel’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu.

Berdasarkan laporan, in the same interview, the president also sought to deflect blame from himself for the losses by republican candidates for the us senate in at least nine states he visited for campaign rallies in the closing weeks of the midterm campaign: north carolina, south carolina, georgia, mississippi, texas, kansas, iowa, michigan and ohio. (He also visited Alaska to campaign for the Republican incumbent, who seems to be on track to lose as well. ).

Asked by Smith what happened in the elections, Trump pointed to the candidates and reminded Smith that he won all of those states as a presidential candidate two years ago (before his popularity plummeted as a result of his decision to raise the cost of goods and fuel for Americans by imposing tariffs on imports and then attacking Iran).

Berdasarkan laporan, he then suggested that he was still popular in all of those formerly republican states that responded to his rallies by voting to reject the candidates he campaigned for. “I think I still have it,” Trump told Smith. “You saw with the rallies, I mean, the rallies were packed. We’d have 15, 20, 25,000 people at every rally,” he added, repeating a false claim he made at most of those rallies, which were, in fact, held in smaller venues, not all of which were filled to capacity.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in san antonio, texas, for instance, a spokesperson for the the venue trump spoke at, freeman coliseum, told reporters the white house requested a three-quarter-house setup, so the hall was set up with 6,844 seats. In Port Huron, Michigan, he packed a small hockey arena with a capacity of 3,000 people. In Greenville, North Carolina, he spoke to 5,000 people at the Pitt-Greenville Airport a fire marshal told the local News & Observer. In Chillicothe, Ohio, Trump claimed that there were 42,000 people in attendance at a university sports center that holds 2,400 spectators.

Taking time out of his busy schedule of posting on social media, Donald Trump sat down for a lengthy podcast interview on Thursday with the sports pundit Stephen A Smith to express sympathy for Jensen Huang, who resigned as chief executive of Nvidia after reports of extramarital affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two company employees.

Diungkapkan bahwa asked by smith, a bombastic commentator who has floated the idea of entering politics himself, if huang should have stepped down, trump sighed deeply before saying: “well, the big thing is, was the woman a spy? and i don’t know if that’s been determined yet, but if the woman was a spy, yes. If the woman was not a spy, perhaps it would be different. ”.

Trump also defended Huang, who sat at his table at a White House state dinner for China’s president, Xi Jinping, in September as “a tremendous talent”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i can tell you this, somehow he’ll end up in his feet,” trump added. I always thought of him as a fine man. “I mean, I know him; I know him pretty well. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i spoke to him yesterday,” he president continued. “He’s he’s going through hell. ”.

“He called me as the president – I’m president – and he called me and he said, ‘What I’ve done to my wife and family is, is- that’s what he talked about,” Trump told Smith.

A return to normal politics: Darline Graham meets with South Carolina senator-elect Annie Andrews.

During the final stretch of South Carolina’s Senate race, Darline Graham laced into her Democratic opponent Annie Andrews, calling her “bat shit crazy,” at a rally with Donald Trump, in what came off as a feeble attempt to match the president’s bravado.

After Andrews’s stunning win, in a seat left vacant by Graham’s late brother, Lindsey Graham, the two appear to be civil.

Graham smiled as she stood next to Andrews, in a Thursday photograph on X.

“I am committed to ensuring a smooth transition, and I wish her and her team the best,” Graham captioned the post.

Democrat Cindy Holscher has been elected Kansas’ next governor, narrowly defeating Republican Ty Masterson to keep the office in her party’s hands and extend a massive wave of Democratic victories across the country.

Democrats had already secured a majority of governorships in US states for the first time in two decades, even prior to the narrow win in Kansas, where Holscher had already declared victory but the Associated Press did not call the race until Thursday.

Diungkapkan bahwa holscher, a state senator, promised to halt new data centers and overcame a flood of money that republicans poured behind masterson, the president of the republican-controlled state senate. She will succeed outgoing governor Laura Kelly, a Democrat who was barred from running for a third term by term limits.

Kelly, a centrist Democrat, had opposed the more progressive Holscher in the Democratic primary, and endorsed her rival, state senators Ethan Corson, but campaigned for the party’s nominee in the general election.

In a campaign ad supporting Holscher last month, Kelly described Masteron as an extremist and assured voters the Democrat would “govern from the middle”.

Masterson, who was endorsed by Donald Trump, remains the Kansas state senate’s Republican leader.

Retaining the governor’s mansion was the third in a series of big wins for Kansas Democrats, after Adam Hamilton was elected to the US Senate, defeating the Trump-backed incumbent Roger Marshall, and Chris Mann defeated the state’s incumbent Republican attorney general Kris Kobach.

Kobach has helped sow doubt about US elections and served as vice-chair of Trump’s short-lived commission on election fraud in 2017, when he tried, and failed, to find evidence to support Trump’s baseless claim that he had not lost the popular vote in the 2016 election.

Mann, a former police officer, had narrowly lost to Kobach in 2022.

Rob Sand, the governor-elect of Iowa, said Democrats should be cautious about spending too much time pursuing Trump administration investigations, claiming voters want to see progress, not rehashing of old wounds.

Berdasarkan laporan, “every time i read, right now, about more investigations of things that have already been reported on in the media, i’m thinking, why do we need to investigate that? it’s already been reported on. Why don’t you do something actually productive or better people’s lives,” Sand told reporters on Thursday in Denver at the What’s Next conference on the future of the Democratic party.

Sand recalled that while serving in the Iowa State Auditor’s office, the team typically did not pursue investigations that had been fully reported on because the public was already aware of potential corruption or misuse of taxpayer funds.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i think that’s a pretty simple guideline for people,” sand said. “Put your time into doing something that’s actually going to improve people’s lives and not just remind them of a bad thing that the other side did. ”.

Sand, who largely campaigned on a platform of being independent and called for the end of the two-party system, said he’s chosen to come to the What’s Next conference because he liked the organization behind it, Majority Democrats.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i’m here for a day,” sand said. “I think it’s important to talk about what we did in Iowa and anytime I can spread the message about making politics, making government, not redder or bluer, but redder and truer, I want to take that opportunity. ”.

While votes are still being counted in one tightly contested Senate election, the race in Alaska where Democrat Mary Peltola now holds a 3,975 vote lead over the nearest Dan Sullivan – the one who is the Republican incumbent – the outgoing Republican majority in Washington is using its final weeks in charge to stack the federal courts with as many judges nominated by Donald Trump as possible.

The Senate has already voted on Thursday to confirm one conservative, Gregory Cook, to be a US district judge in Alabama, and to move to final votes on Trump’s nominations of two judges he previously installed on the federal bench – Daniel Domenico and Anna St John – to serve on federal appeals courts.

The vote on St John’s nomination began with a flub by the senator presiding over the Senate, Darline Graham, the South Carolina Republican who is still serving out the remainder of her late brother Lindsey’s term, which ends in January, despite losing the seat to Democrat Annie Andrews last week.

Sebagaimana diketahui, reading aloud from a piece of paper in front of her, graham called the vote to end debate on st john’s nomination by mistaking the abbreviation for saint in her name, with the one for street. “The question is,” Graham said, “is it the sense of the Senate that debate on the nomination of Anna Street John of Louisiana to be United States judge for the fifth circuit shall be brought to a close?”.

The Alliance for Justice (AFJ), a progressive judicial advocacy group, strongly opposed all three nominees.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, cook, who worked as a volunteer attorney in the 2000 bush v gore legal battle, is described by the afj as “a lifelong conservative who has consistently aligned himself with extremist ideologies in pursuit of more political power” whose “track record demonstrates a commitment to corporate interests and the spread of conservative ideology — not justice. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, domenico, who is described by the afj as a potential supreme court nominee, was nominated to the us district court in colorado by trump in 2019. This year, Trump picked him to serve on the US court of appeals for the 10th circuit in Denver.

Diungkapkan bahwa in january, when trump nominated anna st john to serve as a federal judge for the us district court for the eastern district of louisiana, the afj wrote that she “has spent her legal career silencing women, attacking lgbtq+ rights, and cutting off corporate accountability for everyday people. ” Before being confirmed to that role, and then nominated to a federal appeals court in New Orleans, St John led the Hamilton Legal Law Institute, which the AFJ calls “a far-right extremist organization that routinely files lawsuits to attack civil rights, undermine consumer protections, eliminate gender equality, and deny basic human rights”.

In her confirmation hearing for her elevation the the appeals court in August, St John refused to say that Trump lost the 2020 election and refrained from characterizing the January 6 2021 Capitol riot as an insurrection.

Democrats from across the country have gathered at the What’s Next conference in Denver to discuss what the party should do moving forward – now that they’ve secured majorities in the US House and Senate, and won control of the governor’s offices in a majority of states.

Diungkapkan bahwa the conference, hosted by the group majority democrats, is bustling with excitement. In the outdoor space, there’s a six-piece jazz band playing upbeat variations of Americana songs, flanked by a colorful food truck.

The main stage event will be livestreamed, starting at 2:30 Mountain Time.

In the further annals of Donald Trump not changing a thing since last week’s midterm election defeat, he also mused earlier today on Truth Social: “Will the Seditious Six ever be prosecuted?”.

“What they did was a great violation to our Country and its Constitution!” the president added.

It’s a reference to six Democratic lawmakers who last year published a video reminding members of the military and intelligence community that they can refuse illegal orders, amid concerns that Trump would attempt to use them against his political adversaries.

Here’s what senator Mark Kelly had to say about Trump’s latest threat:.

Berdasarkan laporan, double quotation markthe american people delivered a massive rejection of donald trump’s chaos and corruption last week. Now he’s again threatening to prosecute people who stand up to him because he’s afraid of being held accountable. Donald Trump has tried and failed to intimidate me for a year now. His threats won’t stop me from doing my job.

Immediately after Republicans suffered a drubbing in last week’s midterms, Donald Trump made some comments indicating he’d considering working with the incoming Democratic majorities in the Senate and House of Representatives.

Sebagaimana diketahui, just about everything he’s done since – from appointing immigration hardliner stephen miller his chief of staff to threatening one of the top democratic investigators – indicates he’s not looking to change much at all. Further evidence arrived this afternoon in the form of a Truth Social post, where the president says he’d like to work with Chuck Schumer on fighting corruption – but only in states led by Democrats.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “billions of dollars are being stolen on an hourly basis. Hopefully his words will ring true! It will be an honor to work with him on this very big Democrat problem that, when solved, will literally balance the Budget of the U. S. ” the president writes.

Berdasarkan laporan, little he writes in that sentence appears to be true. There are 8,760 hours in a year, and the Government Accountability Office estimated in 2024 that between $233 bn to $521 bn are lost to fraud annually – so certainly not billions “on an hourly basis,” as Trump wrote. Meanwhile, there are unanswered questions around how Trump has gone about increasing his wealth since he’s been president:.

Berdasarkan laporan, democrats may have ridden voter concerns over the war with iran to their largest congressional majority in years in last week’s midterm elections, but donald trump today announced that the us is no longer bothering to find peace with its middle eastern adversary. Here’s more, from the Guardian’s Andrew Roth:.

Donald Trump has said that the US is no longer seeking a deal to end the war with Iran and ordered JD Vance, who had spearheaded recent efforts to restart negotiations with Iran, to focus on domestic politics instead.

Berdasarkan laporan, in a post to his social media site on thursday, trump said he was redirecting the vice-president to focus his “complete and total attention on the massive corruption and crime taking place in democrat run cities and states throughout the u. S”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, vance had reportedly been talking to intermediaries in iran and qatar about restarting negotiations to end the war, which began in february when the us and israel launched joint strikes on iran. Iran responded by closing access to the strait of Hormuz, which led to a steep increase for the cost of fuel around the globe.

But on Thursday Trump appeared to shut down the negotiations, redirecting Vance to focus on domestic issues and downplaying the need for a final deal.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we don’t need a deal with iran,” trump wrote. “Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!”.

We reported earlier that Ukraine’s president has said that Starlink, the satellite internet service it relies to counter Russian drone attacks, has slowed down, hampering its defenses.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, democrats are already expected to investigate a number of the activities of elon musk, who controls starlink, and whether the service is being deliberately throttled for ukraine could be on their list. While many of these inquiries are sure to be strictly partisan affairs, Michael McCaul, an outgoing House Republican who supports defending Ukraine against Russia, just signaled his support for this particular line of questioning, writing the following on X:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, double quotation marki am deeply concerned by reports that ukraine’s access to starshield has once again been restricted. These capabilities play a critical role in Ukraine’s defense against Putin’s relentless missile and drone attacks, which target civilian homes, parks, hospitals, and energy infrastructure.

Diungkapkan bahwa with peace negotiations on the horizon, maintaining ukraine’s momentum and leverage is more important than ever. I urge a full investigation into why these disruptions have now occurred twice and call for measures be put in place to ensure it does not happen again.

Sebagaimana diketahui, donald trump’s health secretary, robert f kennedy jr, is facing potential legal trouble after a democratic senator opened an inquiry into whether the lied to congress, citing reporting by the guardian. Here’s more, from the Guardian’s Michelle R Smith:.

A top Democratic senator has launched an investigation into evidence that Robert F Kennedy Jr “unlawfully lied” in his 2025 confirmation hearings to become the US health secretary, citing a report by the Guardian.

Ron Wyden of Oregon, the incoming chair of the powerful Senate finance committee, is seeking extensive records from Children’s Health Defense (CHD), the non-profit anti-vaccine group Kennedy has used as a vehicle to fuel his political rise, including all documents related to a 2019 trip Kennedy took to Samoa.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we are beginning an investigation into evidence that secretary of health and human services robert f kennedy, jr unlawfully lied to congress on multiple occasions,” wyden said in a letter to the group that was sent on wednesday and obtained by the guardian. The letter was also signed by Angela Alsobrooks, a Democratic senator from Maryland.

In the letter, the two lawmakers cited reporting by the Guardian that indicated Kennedy lied about his reasons for going to Samoa in 2019, a trip that occurred just months before a measles outbreak killed 83 people in the Pacific island nation, mostly children under age five.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the trip, which kennedy made as the chair and chief legal counsel of chd, became one of the most criticized events in his career before he entered government. Critics, including Samoan officials, have said Kennedy’s presence emboldened anti-vaccine activists in Samoa, worsening a vaccination crisis. Kennedy has denied the allegations, saying he never gave any public statement about vaccines or discouraged Samoans from getting vaccinated.

The Trump administration faces an investigation of its scheme to take a 15% cut from any Nvidia chip sales going to China, as part of a deal to secure export licenses for the semiconductors.

Berdasarkan laporan, under the scheme, nvidia chips made in taiwan could be sold to chinese companies if they were imported to the us first for a security review. This also made them subject to a 25% tariff under section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, which was aimed at dealing with imports that threaten national security. The commerce secretary could then grant an export licence to sell the chips to China.

Two Democratic senators are now demanding Trump officials retain all records relating to the scheme as the fallout from now former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy continues to grow.

Diungkapkan bahwa senate finance committee ranking member ron wyden and house ways and means committee ranking member richard e. Neal said they were beginning to investigate following reports of the affair – which led to Huang’s resignation on Thursday. One focus of the investigation appear to be report that both commerce secretary Howard Lutnick and Donald Trump were briefed about the relationship but granted export approvals anyway.

double quotation markThe Trump administration’s ostensible attempt to mask an unconstitutional export tax as a national security tariff action – benefitting both Nvidia and the Chinese government – raises serious concerns within our committees’ jurisdiction over matters relating to taxation and tariffs.

Congress wrote Section 232 to give the president a tool to take action against imports he has determined to pose a national security threat; Trump’s use of the statute appears to have done the opposite, undermining US national security and putting Americans at risk.

#204. A new approach to a Covid-19 nasal vaccine shows early promise

📅 03 Apr 2023

A new approach to a Covid-19 nasal vaccine shows early promise

Tanggal: 03 Apr 2023 | Sumber: https://www.cnn.com/2023/04/03/health/nasal-vaccine-sterilizing-immunity/index.html

Scientists in Germany say they’ve been able to make a nasal vaccine that can shut down a Covid-19 infection in the nose and throat, where the virus gets its first foothold in the body.

In experiments in hamsters, two doses of the vaccine – which is made with a live but weakened form of the coronavirus that causes Covid-19 – blocked the virus from copying itself in the animals’ upper airways, achieving “sterilizing immunity” and preventing illness, a long-sought goal of the pandemic.

WHO experts revise Covid-19 vaccine advice, say healthy kids and teens low risk.

Although this vaccine has several more hurdles to clear before it gets to a doctor’s office or drug store, other nasal vaccines are in use or are nearing the finish line in clinical trials.

Diungkapkan bahwa china and india both rolled out vaccines given through the nasal tissues last fall, though it’s not clear how well they may be working. Studies on the effectiveness of these vaccines have yet to be published, leaving much of the world to wonder whether this approach to protection really works in people.

Diungkapkan bahwa the us has reached something of a stalemate with covid-19. Even with the darkest days of the pandemic behind us, hundreds of Americans are still dying daily as the infection continues to simmer in the background of our return to normal life.

Diungkapkan bahwa as long as the virus continues to spread among people and animals, there’s always the potential for it mutate into a more contagious or more damaging version of itself. And while Covid infections have become manageable for most healthy people, they may still pose a danger to vulnerable groups such as the elderly and immunocompromised.

Researchers hope next-generation Covid-19 vaccines, which aim to shut down the virus before it ever gets a chance to make us sick and ultimately prevent the spread of infection, could make our newest resident respiratory infection less of a threat.

China approves its first mRNA Covid-19 vaccine.

One way scientists are trying to do that is by boosting mucosal immunity, beefing up immune defenses in the tissues that line the upper airways, right where the virus would land and begin to infect our cells.

It’s a bit like stationing firefighters underneath the smoke alarm in your house, says study author Emanuel Wyler, a scientist at the Max Delbruck Center for Molecular Medicine in the Helmholtz Association in Berlin.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the immunity that’s created by shots works throughout the body, but it resides primarily in the blood. That means it may take longer to mount a response.

“If they are already on site, they can immediately eliminate the fire, but if they’re like 2 miles away, they first need to drive there, and by that time, one-third of the house is already in full flames,” Wyler said.

Diungkapkan bahwa mucosal vaccines are also better at priming a different kind of first responder than injections do. They do a better job of summoning IgA antibodies, which have four arms to grab onto invaders instead of the two arms that the y-shaped IgG antibodies have. Some scientists think IgA antibodies may be less picky about their targets than IgG antibodies, which makes them better equipped to deal with new variants.

Diungkapkan bahwa the new nasal vaccine takes a new approach to a very old idea: weakening a virus so it’s no longer a threat and then giving it to people so their immune systems can learn to recognize and fight it off. The first vaccines using this approach date to the 1870s, against anthrax and rabies. Back then, scientists weakened the agents they were using with heat and chemicals.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the researchers manipulated the genetic material in the virus to make it harder for cells to translate. This technique, called codon pair deoptimization, hobbles the virus so it can be shown to the immune system without making the body sick.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “you could imagine reading a text … and every letter is a different font, or every letter is a different size, then the text is much harder to read. And this is basically what we do in codon pair deoptimization,” Wyler said.

In the hamster studies, which were published Monday in the journal Nature Microbiology, two doses of the live but weakened nasal vaccine created a much stronger immune response than either two doses of an mRNA-based vaccine or one that uses an adenovirus to ferry the vaccine instructions into cells.

The researchers think the live weakened vaccine probably worked better because it closely mimics the process of a natural infection.

The nasal vaccine also previews the entire coronavirus for the body, not just its spike proteins like current Covid-19 vaccines do, so the hamsters were able to make immune weapons against a wider range of targets.

Diungkapkan bahwa as promising as all this sounds, vaccine experts say caution is warranted. This vaccine still has to pass more tests before it’s ready for use, but they say the results look encouraging.

Health officials consider another round of bivalent boosters for the most vulnerable Americans.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “they did a very nice job. This is obviously a competent and thoughtful team that did this work, and impressive in the scope of what they did. Greg Poland, who designs vaccines at the Mayo Clinic. Now it just needs to be repeated,” perhaps in primates and certainly in humans before it can be widely used, said Dr. He was not involved in the new research.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the study began in 2021, before the omicron variant was around, so the vaccine tested in these experiments was made with the original strain of the coronavirus. In the experiments, when they infected animals with Omicron, the live but weakened nasal vaccine still performed better than the others, but its ability to neutralize the virus was diminished. Berdasarkan laporan, editor’s note:  a version of this story first appeared in cnn’s meanwhile in the middle east newsletter, a three-times-a-week look inside the region’s biggest stories. Sign up here.

Turkey’s persecuted pro-Kurdish party has emerged as a kingmaker in the country’s upcoming election, playing a decisive role that may just tip the balance enough to unseat two-decade ruler Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

In a key setback to the Turkish president and leader of the Justice and Development Party (AK Party), the pro-Kurdish Peoples’ Democratic Party (HDP) last month announced that it would not put forward its own presidential candidate, a move analysts say allows its supporters to vote for Erdogan’s main rival.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we are facing a turning point that will shape the future of turkey and (its) society,” said the hdp in a statement on march 23. “To fulfill our historical responsibility against the one-man rule, we will not field a presidential candidate in (the) May 14 elections. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa it is a twist of irony for the turkish strongman, who spent the better half of the past decade cracking down on the party after it began chipping away at his voter base. Its former leader Selahattin Demirtas has been in prison for nearly seven years and the party faces possible closure by a court for suspected collusion with the militant Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK) and affiliated groups. But its influence may nonetheless determine the course of Turkey’s politics.

Berdasarkan laporan, the hdp’s decision not to field a candidate came just three days after head of the republican people’s party (chp) kemal kilicdaroglu, erdogan’s main rival, visited the party’s co-chairs. He told reporters that the solution to Turkey’s problems, “including the Kurdish problem” lies in parliament,” according to Turkish media.

Berdasarkan laporan, kilicdaroglu, who represents the six-party nation alliance opposition bloc, is the strongest contender to run against erdogan in years. And while the HDP hasn’t yet announced whether it will put its weight behind him, analysts say it is the kingmaker in the elections.

Erdogan's 'polar opposite' wants to replace him as president of Turkey.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it was a carefully crafted political discourse,” hisyar ozsoy, deputy co-chair of the hdp and a member of parliament from the predominantly kurdish province of diyarbakir, told cnn. “We are not going to have our own candidate, and we will leave it to the international community to interpret it the way they wish. ”.

Experts say the crackdown on the HDP is rooted in the threat it poses to Erdogan politically, as well as its position as one of the main parties representing Turkey’s Kurds, an ethnic minority from which a separatist militant movement has emerged.

Diungkapkan bahwa the party and the kurdish people have had a complicated relationship with erdogan. The leader courted the Kurds in earlier years by granting them more rights and reversing restrictions on the use of their language. Relations with the HDP were also cordial once, as Erdogan worked with the party on a brief peace process with the PKK.

But ties between Erdogan and the HDP later turned sour, and the HDP fell under a sweeping crackdown aimed at the PKK and their affiliates.

Kurds are the biggest minority in Turkey, making up between 15% and 20% of the population, according to Minority Rights Group International.

It is unclear if the HDP will endorse Kilicdaroglu, but analysts say that the deliberate distance may be beneficial for the opposition candidate.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the accusations against the hdp place it in a precarious position during the elections. It currently faces a case in Turkey’s Constitutional Court over suspected ties to the PKK, which is designated as a terrorist group by Turkey, the United States and the European Union. Knowing it may be banned at any moment, its candidates are running under the Green Left Party in parliament.

If the opposition is seen as allying with the HDP, Erdogan’s AK Party may use its influence in the media to discredit it as being pro-PKK, said Murat Somer, a political science professor at Koc University in Istanbul and author of Return to Point Zero, a book on the Turkish-Kurdish question in Turkey.

Berdasarkan laporan, the hdp’s threat to erdogan’s hold on power became apparent after the june 2015 election, the first general election it participated in. It won 13% of the seats, denying the ruling AK Party its majority for the first time since 2002. Erdogan, however, called a snap election five months later, which led to a drop in the HDP’s support to 10. 7%, as well as the restoration of the AK Party’s overall majority.

Diungkapkan bahwa “they are a kingmaker in these elections because the hdp gets about half of the votes of the kurdish population in turkey,” said somer, adding that the other, more conservative kurdish voters have traditionally voted for erdogan’s ak party. And last month, the Free Cause Party (HUDA-PAR), a tiny Kurdish-Islamist party announced support for Erdogan in the elections. The party has never won seats in parliament.

Erdogan's political fate may rest on his response to the earthquake.

The HDP knows that its position is key to the outcome of next month’s vote, but that it’s also in a delicate situation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we want to play the game wisely, and we need to be very careful,” said ozsoy, adding that the party wants to avoid a “contaminated political climate” where the elections are polarized “between a very ugly ultra-nationalist discourse against kilicdaroglu and others. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the party was founded in 2012 with a number of aims, said ozsoy, one of which was “peaceful and democratic resolution of the kurdish conflict. ”.

Somer said that the party was seen to be “an initiative” of the PKK, which later led to a heavy government crackdown on it in the name of counterterrorism.

Its former leader Demirtas remains an influential figure.

The Turkish government has been trying to link the HDP to the PKK but has so far failed to prove “a real connection,” said Asli Aydintasbas, a visiting fellow at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a post-erdogan turkey may give some breathing space to the kurds and kurdish-dominated parties in turkey, aydintasbas told cnn, noting that many kurdish voters have recently left erdogan’s camp. “It’s a matter of survival. “For HDP, this is more than just an ideological choice,” she said. ”.

Ozsoy says his party understands what’s at stake, not only for Turkey’s Kurds but for all its minorities.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we are aware of our responsibility here. We are aware of our role. We know we are in a kingmaker position,” the HDP lawmaker said.

Americans have grown used to corporate executives treading the well-worn paths of the Northeast corridor to convene alongside elected officials in Washington, DC, and discuss geopolitics, policy and all that’s in-between.

Diungkapkan bahwa in 2017, major ceos from across the country came together to oppose north carolina’s transgender bathroom law. In 2019, they called abortion bans “bad for business. ”.

After the deadly attack on the US Capitol on January 6, 2021, many of corporate America’s biggest names denounced the rioters and pledged to halt their political giving.

Recently, more than 1,000 companies promised to voluntarily curtail their operations in Russia in protest of Moscow’s war on Ukraine.

Dick’s Sporting Goods stopped selling semi-automatic, assault-style rifles at stores and Citigroup put new restrictions on gun sales by business customers after the mass shooting at a high school in Parkland, Florida, in 2018.

A year later, after mass shootings at a Walmart in El Paso, Texas, and a nightclub in Dayton, Ohio, Walmart ended handgun ammunition sales.

Corporate leadership has long been vocal on the issue of gun control – in 2019 and again this past summer nearly 150 major companies – including Lululemon, Lyft, Bain Capital, Bloomberg LP, Permanente Medical Group and Unilever – called gun violence a “public health crisis” and demanded that the US Senate pass legislation to address it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that’s why corporate america’s silence in the wake of the latest mass shooting at a school in nashville is so jarring. The United States has come to rely on the increasing power of large corporations as political advocates.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but yale professor jeffrey sonnenfeld, a vocal advocate of corporate social responsibility who has a direct line to major ceos around the globe, said that top executives are forlorn. Their previous efforts haven’t done much to push the needle on gun control legislation and without more backing, they don’t know what else they can do at the moment, he said.

Before the Bell spoke with Sonnenfeld, who runs Yale School of Management’s Chief Executive Leadership Institute, a nonprofit educational and research institute focused on CEO leadership and corporate governance.

This interview has been edited for clarity and length.

Before the Bell: CEOs have been quiet about gun reform since the latest mass school shooting in Nashville, have you heard anything about plans to speak out?.

Berdasarkan laporan, jeffrey sonnenfeld: where is everybody else? where is all of civil society? ceos are just one group of people and it’s like we’re turning to them to be our saviors on every topic. They’ve joined causes with valor and nobility but they can’t just be taking cause after cause as if there’s nobody else in society. We saw campuses alive and aroused. The social change that happened in the 1960s wasn’t being led primarily by CEOs. Social changes really happened when we saw the interfaith activity of clergy locking arms and canvassing legislators. Where’s all the student activism?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the ceos are still the most active even if they’re less active than they were six months ago. They’re not there as hired hands of shareholders to fill the role of politicians and civic leaders. They’re there to join that chorus, but they don’t want to be the only one singing.

So is this what you’re hearing from top CEOs? Have they gotten tired of advocating?.

Diungkapkan bahwa i just got off of a ceo call on voting rights and this morning we had a forum on sustainability – ceos are still the most active on these fronts. It’s the same thing on immigration reform. If a CEO was working an 18 hour day on a 12 day week, they still couldn’t address all of the issues that need addressing.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the nation’s ceos are waiting for everybody else to join them. They don’t need to restate something they’ve already stated. They’ve jumped in the pool, where’s everybody else?.

So what do you think has led to this complacency amongst Americans and the growing reliance on CEOs to advocate on our behalf?.

Diungkapkan bahwa they’ve taken a very strong stance and they’ve gone out further than the general public. Enough already on saying ‘what are the CEOs doing?’ Social capital is as valuable as financial capital. CEOs understand that in their soul, they want there to be social capital. They want there to be public trust, but they need the rest of civil society to join them. They are where the general public is on surveys, but they’re not where the general public is on action in the streets. So we’re ready for others to now do something. And that’s their frustration.

But don’t these CEOs hold the purse strings in terms of donating to powerful politicians?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, you would think that, but since the 2020 elections much less of campaign contributions have come from big business. Since the 2021 run on the Capitol, a lot of businesses either had an official moratorium or they’ve given mere pennies to politicians. The common impression on the street that CEOs are controlling campaign purses strings is 100% wrong.

Diungkapkan bahwa tesla reported. a modest 4% rise in sales in the first quarter compared to the final three months of last year, despite a series of price cuts on its lower priced vehicles and talk by CEO Elon Musk about strong demand at those lower prices.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the first quarter also marked the fourth straight quarter that tesla has produced more vehicles than it has delivered to customers. Some of that may be due to the ramp up in production at two new factories, one in Texas, the other in Germany, which opened last spring, and a lag between that increased production and sales.

Tesla said there was an increase in the number of its more expensive models, the Model S and Model X, in transit to Europe, the Middle East and Africa, as well as to the Asia Pacific region.

But it does mean that over the last 12 months Tesla has produced 78,000 more cars than it has sold, suggesting that talk of strong demand by Tesla executives may not be backed up by the numbers.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “early this year, we had a price adjustment. “And as Elon said, as long as you offer a product with value at affordable price, you don’t have to worry about demand. After that, we actually generated a huge demand, more than we can produce, really,” said Tom Zhu, Tesla’s executive in charge of global production and sales. ”.

#241. What pet cemeteries reveal about being human

📅 03 Apr 2023

What pet cemeteries reveal about being human

Tanggal: 03 Apr 2023 | Sumber: https://www.cnn.com/2023/04/03/opinions/pet-cemeteries-burying-animals-history-tourigny/index.html

Diungkapkan bahwa editor’s note:  eric tourigny is a lecturer in historical archaeology at newcastle university, uk. His research interprets osteological and material culture remains alongside historic texts to examine changing human-animal relationships in Europe and North America over the past 500 years. The views expressed in this commentary are his own. Read more opinion on CNN.

Berdasarkan laporan, why do we bury our departed loved ones in a cemetery? a primary purpose is to provide survivors with an opportunity to grieve and gain a sense of closure. The cemetery is a place for the living as much as it is a place for the dead.

But what about when the dearly departed are not human – but our pets?.

Diungkapkan bahwa the spanish city of barcelona recently announced that it will be investing in the establishment of the country’s first public pet cemetery. Set to open next year, it will offer both burials and cremations – with an estimated 7,000 carried out each year.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for me, as someone who has spent years researching the development of pet cemeteries elsewhere in the world, this news came as a shock. Barcelona is a densely populated city with limited privately owned land – one where 50% of families own a pet.

Berdasarkan laporan, how did a city that is home to 180,000 dogs not already have a public pet cemetery? until now, the service was only provided by the private sector, according to barcelona’s councilor for climate emergency and ecological transition, eloi badia. He added that the municipal-funded initiative was sparked by “constant public demand. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, after all, public pet cemeteries have been around in europe and the americas since the late 19th century. Britain’s first public pet cemetery appeared in London’s Hyde Park in 1881. New York’s Hartsdale pet cemetery was founded in 1896, followed a few years later by Paris’ ornate Cimetière des Chiens in 1899.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i became interested in the history of modern pet burial practices while investigating the archaeological record of a centuries-old house in toronto. I came across a (very) large dog buried in the back garden which, according to the historical record, was occupied between 1840 and 1870.

Berdasarkan laporan, this dog survived to an elderly age but, sadly, suffered from degenerative joint disease and severe infections during his last months. His ailments progressed to such a state that suggest he received some level of care in his final weeks. He then was buried in a personal plot behind the family home.

Berdasarkan laporan, this elderly dog led me to think about the different ways people interact with the bodies of their pets after death. Could this behavior be reflective of the relationships they held with their animals in life? In this instance, why take the time to carefully bury a dog in its own space when other, arguably easier options existed?.

This, after all, was an era when people often disposed of their dead pets in the river, or might have sold their bodies for meat and skin.

Good hygiene is an obvious reason to choose a burial – no one wants decomposing animal bodies in the street or their garden – but that wouldn’t immediately warrant a personalized, dedicated burial and gravestone.

Diungkapkan bahwa the most straight forward option would be to dispose of a deceased animal with the household waste. But such treatment would evidently feel less ceremonious and would not offer appropriate emotional closure to what was likely an important relationship.

Like the burial of people, the burial of pets is an intimate cultural practice, one that changes over time and is reflective of the changing relationships that a society has with its cherished creatures.

Sebagaimana diketahui, my study of historic gravestones and epitaphs in britain from the victorian period to today shows this changing human-animal relationship. In the 19th century, gravestones were often dedicated to a “loving friend” or “devoted companion,” suggesting pets were mostly considered important friends.

Berdasarkan laporan, by the early 20th century, pets had become members of the family – evidenced by the appearance of family surnames on the gravestones, and loving epitaphs written by “mummy and daddy. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa by the early 20th century, pets had become members of the family – evidenced by the appearance of family surnames on the gravestones, and loving epitaphs written by “mummy and daddy. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, society’s changing attitude towards the role of animals in the afterlife can also be found. Fast-forward a few decades later, and gravestones were more likely to reference a reunion then earlier ones. For example, the owners of Denny, the “brave little cat” buried in an east London cemetery in 1952, wrote on his epitaph “God bless until we meet again. ”.

I wonder what the epitaphs in Barcelona’s new cemetery will reveal about modern Catalan relationships with animals.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, over time, our ways of treating our animal dead appear to reflect an even closer relationship in life. Once strictly forbidden by law, the last decade saw many jurisdictions, like the state of New York, allowing the co-burial of cremated animals and people, which will undoubtedly lead to changing funerary and commemoration practices for both humans and animals.

For me, the most remarkable similarity between modern and historic pet cemeteries is the striking evidence for the heartbreak and taboos around grieving for animals.

Berdasarkan laporan, the connection that someone has with their pet can be just as strong and just as significant as their relationships with other humans. Yet today, as in over 100 years ago, individuals continue to struggle to find the appropriate outlet to express their pain, hiding heartache for fear of the social repercussions that might come with public acknowledgment of the existence of such a bond.

Berdasarkan laporan, the rspca reassures the public on its website that they should not feel shame for their grief. In the UK, charities like the Blue Cross and Rainbow Bridge Pet Loss Grief Center offer counseling to bereaved humans.

Diungkapkan bahwa close relationships between people and animals have existed for millennia, but in western european cultures, there were few acceptable ways to mourn that relationship. As society becomes more accepting of the importance of human-animal relationships to our collective wellbeing, it is not surprising to see us follow rituals resembling those we use to mourn the loss of our closest human relationships.

At an estimated cost of €200 ($217) per service at the new Barcelona cemetery, it is important to acknowledge that this opportunity to grieve will not be financially available to everyone in the city.

Berdasarkan laporan, this will not be a space for all of the city’s pets. Pet owners may opt to keep cremated remains within their home or spread out ashes in a meaningful location instead. Online forums and digital pet cemeteries also provide other opportunities to commemorate the relationship and express grief.

Whether one chooses a pet cemetery or not, there are many acceptable ways to express your grief – and to remember your relationship with the important animals in your life.

#244. Scientists film deepest ever fish on seabed off Japan

📅 03 Apr 2023

Scientists film deepest ever fish on seabed off Japan

Tanggal: 03 Apr 2023 | Sumber: https://www.cnn.com/2023/04/03/asia/deepest-fish-filmed-off-japan-scn-intl-hnk/index.html

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sign up for cnn’s wonder theory science newsletter. Explore the universe with news on fascinating discoveries, scientific advancements and more.

Cruising at a depth of 8,336 meters (over 27,000 feet) just above the seabed, a young snailfish has become the deepest fish ever filmed by scientists during a probe into the abyss of the northern Pacific Ocean.

Scientists from University of Western Australia and Tokyo University of Marine Science and Technology released footage of the snailfish on Sunday filmed last September by sea robots in deep trenches off Japan.

Along with the filming the deepest snailfish, the scientists physically caught two other specimens at 8,022 meters and set another record for the deepest catch.

Previously, the deepest snailfish ever spotted was at 7,703 meters in 2008, while scientists had never been able to collect fish from anywhere below 8,000 meters.

“What is significant is that it shows how far a particular type of fish will descend in the ocean,” said marine biologist Alan Jamieson, founder of the Minderoo-UWA Deep Sea Research Centre, who led the expedition.

Berdasarkan laporan, scientists are filming in the trenches off japan as part of a 10-year study into the deepest fish populations in the world. Snailfish are members of Liparidae family, and while most snailfish live in shallow water, others survive at some of the greatest depths ever recorded, Jamieson said.

During the two-month survey last year, three “landers” – automatic sea robots fitted with high-resolution cameras – were dropped into three trenches – the Japan, Izu-Ogasawara and Ryukyu trenches – at varying depths.

In the Izu-Ogasawara trench, footage showed the deepest snailfish hovering calmly alongside other crustaceans on the seabed.

Jamieson classified the fish as a juvenile and said younger deep sea snailfish often stay as deep as possible to avoid being eaten by bigger predators that swim at shallower depths.

Another clip shot at between 7,500 and 8,200 meters in the same trench showed a colony of fish and crustaceans munching at bait tied to an undersea robot.

Images of the two captured snailfish – identified as Pseudoliparis belyaevi – provide a rare glimpse of the unique features that help the deep sea species survive the extreme environment.

They have tiny eyes, a translucent body, and their lack of swim bladder, which helps other fish float, works to their advantage, Jamieson said.

The professor said the Pacific Ocean is particularly conducive to vibrant activity due to its warm southern current, which encourages sea creatures to go deeper, while its abundant marine life provides a good source of food for bottom feeders.

Scientists would like to know more about creatures living at extreme depths, but cost is the constraint, Jamieson said, adding that each lander alone costs them $200,000 to assemble and operate.

“The challenges are that technology has been expensive and scientists don’t have a lot of money,” he said.
